picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech odds, spread and over/under for Week 9 Skip to main content SI.COM Wildcats in the Pros Brent Brennan and the No. 22 Arizona Wildcats have a crucial Week 9 game on deck, heading to Lubbock to take on the No. 13 Texas Tech Red Raiders on Halloween in a massive Big 12 showdown. A win would give Arizona a 4-1 record in Big 12 play, which would put them no worse than tied for second in the conference heading into Week 10 - and makes them a real dark horse contender for a spot in the College Football Playoff, or at least the Big 12 championship game. Arizona is 2-1 on the road this season, losing in Week 2 to BYU in Provo, but taking care of business against former Pac-12 foe Washington State in Pullman in Week 4 and dismantling West Virginia, 52-31, in Morgantown in Week 6. It has led to an excellent run game for the Red Raiders, who are led by J'Koby Williams and his 619 rushing yards and five touchdowns - good for a whopping 7.2 yards per carry. QB play hasn't been quite as consistent for coach Joey McGuire's club, with Will Hammond completing 67.8% of his passes for 1,561 yards - but only six passing touchdowns with six interceptions to boot. A monster Big 12 matchup hits Halloween as Arizona heads to Texas Tech for a game between two 6-1 squads that will inevitably shake up the standings. My Arizona vs. Texas Tech prediction questions Will Hammond's quality, while my college football picks look at a 54.5-point total that might be too high. This game will be broadcast on ESPN at 12 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. TOP PICK Who will win Arizona vs Texas Tech: Arizona +3.5 Play Arizona at anything +3 or above. Texas Tech has a quarterback problem. Will Hammond has 13 turnover-worthy passes to pair with only eight big-time throws (per PFF), and his limitations have resulted in the third least-explosive passing attack in the nation . That makes them one-dimensional offensively, and it plays into Arizona's run-stopping defense. The Red Raiders don't block well enough up front (118th in front seven havoc allowed) to compensate for the quarterback deficiency. Tech's secondary has been hit for 266.1 passing yards per game, so the Wildcats (10th in passing success rate) will be able to chuck it around. Arizona vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 54.5 Tech's offensive limitations will show through in this matchup. Arizona's defense (14th in EPA per play, 11th in success rate) is much better than the market is accounting for, as it doesn't have name recognition but is well-coordinated under Danny Gonzales. On the flip side, Tech's defense checks in at 16th in EPA per play allowed and 10th in PFF's team defense grade. The strength of this team still resides on that side of the ball, and Joey McGuire will attempt to lean on that unit and minimize possessions for Fifita. Arizona's top three wide receivers have all been out. Tre Spivey is done for the year, while Giovanni Richardson and Chris Hunter III are considered questionable. The Wildcats can still move the ball in the air, but the efficiency won't be at its peak given the cluster injuries. Arizona vs Texas Tech combo Arizona got off to slow starts against Washington State and Northern Illinois, and could do so again during a difficult trip to Lubbock. Texas Tech has cashed the First Half Under in eight of its last 13 games. Given Hammond's turnover-prone ways and overall offensive issues, the defense should be the focal point over the second half of the season. Under 27.5 in the First Half Arizona vs Texas Tech prop: First Quarter Under 10.5 Texas Tech has cashed the Under in the first quarter in 10 of its last 13 games. The offense could struggle out of the gates again, given Arizona's stingy defensive statistics. Arizona's offense has put up big numbers against lower competition, but doing so early on the road against an NIL-aided defense is a different ask. Pictured: Arizona Wildcats quarterback Noah Fifita. Alex Hinton · Action Network Sat, October 31, 2026 at 11:01 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Last week was a very significant one for the Big 12 title race. Utah knocked off Houston as it hosted College Gameday. BYU could not avoid a letdown after beating Notre Dame as it lost at UCF in the Bounce House. However, many likely did not see Texas Tech losing at Cincinnati as a double-digit favorite. The Red Raiders fell to 3-1 in conference play and return home to face Arizona. Typically, Texas Tech, Utah, BYU, and Houston are the teams discussed when people bring up Big 12 Championship and College Football Playoff implications. However, Arizona is not to be slept on, as it is also 3-1 in the conference and sits at No. 22 in the AP Top 25. Arizona is alive and well in the Big 12 race and CFP with shots at Texas Tech and Utah in the next couple of weeks. If they are going to go on that kind of run, it will be led by senior quarterback Noah Fifita . That is where we will begin my Texas Tech vs. Arizona picks and college football parlay for college football Week 9 on Saturday, Oct. 31. Noah Fifita 250+ Alt Passing Yards (-130) Will Hammond 200+ Alt Passing Yards (+102) J'Koby Williams 60+ Alt Rushing Yards (-154) Parlay Odds: +448 ( FanDuel ) Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds As a four-year starter, Noah Fifita has thrown for over 11,000 passing yards and only needs nine touchdowns to reach 100 for his career. However, his senior season is on track to be the best one of his career. Fifita heads into Lubbock this week, completing 74.2% of his passes while throwing for 2,064 yards, 18 touchdowns and just four interceptions. He ranks in the top 20 among FBS quarterbacks in passing yards, touchdown passes and QBR. Fifita is averaging 292.4 passing yards per game this season. He has thrown for 250 yards in six of his first seven games this season and eight of his last nine dating back to last season. He has only faced Texas Tech once in his career, and while he did throw two interceptions, he also threw for 301 yards on 49 attempts. He is coming off consecutive 300-yard games, and a third may be in the cards this week. The Red Raiders are allowing 266.1 passing yards per game, and they have allowed 275 passing yards in four of their past six games. They also rank 86th in passing Success Rate allowed and 106th in explosiveness allowed. Averaging 9.2 yards per attempt this season, Fifita should take advantage. Lost in the Brendan Sorsby saga was the fact that Texas Tech had another starting-caliber quarterback on the roster. Will Hammond was just recovering from a torn ACL. After flashing in spot duty, Hammond has underwhelmed to a degree this season. He has six touchdowns and six interceptions on the year and ranks 51st in QBR. However, he has also thrown for 1,561 yards and is averaging 223 yards per game. Hammond has thrown for 200 yards in five of his seven starts this season, including each of the Red Raiders' four home games. He's averaging 253 passing yards per game at home this season and faces a Wildcats defense that allows 207.7 passing yards per game. It will help Hammond this week having both of his standout running backs available. Cameron Dickey was injured in the victory over Colorado and has missed the Red Raiders' last two games. J'Koby Williams picked up the slack, rushing for 165 yards against Arizona State and 81 at Cincinnati last week. He leads the team with 619 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 7.2 yards per carry. However, even when Dickey has been available, Williams has run for at least 60 yards in four of his five games and six of his seven overall. He will face an Arizona defense that has been strong against the run, ranking 10th in Rushing Success Rate allowed. It's allowing 107.7 rushing yards per game and 3.1 yards per carry. However, the Wildcats are 126th in explosiveness allowed. That should benefit both Hammond and particularly Williams, who has had a 20-yard rush in each of his last six games.

Score prediction for Arizona game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Will Texas Tech football get back on track? Score prediction for Arizona game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Things have taken quite the turn for the Texas Tech football team after suffering its first loss of the season. Getting bested by Cincinnati for 60 minutes has put the Red Raiders in a pressure point. There's little wiggle room left for Joey McGuire's team to keep its hopes of repeating as Big 12 Conference champions alive. Now they have a talented Arizona team coming to Galaxy Stadium looking to kick the Red Raiders while they're down. What will it take for Texas Tech to walk away with the win? Is Arizona actually the favorite in this game? Our breakdown of the game, plus a score prediction. What's holding Texas Tech football back? It's a layered conversation as to what is keeping the Red Raiders from reaching their potential. For starters, the offense, led by quarterback Will Hammond, hasn't put up the kind of numbers Tech fans want. Receivers have struggled to get open (besides Kenny Johnson) and when they do create separation from their defenders, Hammond hasn't found them or delivered solid throws enough to take advantage. While the rushing game has been a point of scorn for some fans, J'Koby Williams has been electric, and Cameron Dickey is on track to rejoin him in the backfield this week. Defensively, the pass defense has been sporadic. The 13 interceptions (second in the nation) and five pick-6s count, but when those haven't come, opponents have had little trouble moving the ball through the air against the Red Raiders. These things have been present all year but only came to a head against Cincinnati. Now they face an Arizona team equipped to exploit these very issues. TEMPE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 25: Quarterback Noah Fifita #11 of the Arizona Wildcats walks out to the field before the NCAAF game against the Arizona State Sun Devils at Mountain America Stadium on November 25, 2023 in Tempe, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) What Arizona football can do to beat Texas Tech football The Wildcats rank sixth in the nation in total sacks (24.0), bringing constant pressure to opposing quarterbacks to get them out of rhythm. Cincinnati generated a season-high four sacks against the Red Raiders last week, while Arizona has three games with five or more sacks. Noah Fifita and the Arizona offense have also been operating at a high level, generating at least 280 yards through the air in six of the team's seven games. Fifita ranks third in the Big 12 with 2,064 passing yards, totaling 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions. The Wildcats have been hit with injuries to their receiving room, having already lost Tre Spivey for the season and seeing two others on the team's first availability report for the game. Even so, Arizona's offense has operated at a high level. Texas Tech football's notable streak on the line The Red Raiders have won their last 12 home games, which ranks one shy of the program record set during World War II when the Red Raiders won 13 straight games from 1939 to 1942. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs. Arizona Arizona 35, Texas Tech 21: This is a pivot point for the Red Raiders to determine where they'll be in the Big 12 title race. Problem is, Texas Tech struggled to generate offense against a bad Cincinnati defense, and Arizona's defense has been quality all season. Bad recipe. picks.headline: Texas Tech-Arizona football predictions: Who wins Big 12 Top 25 showdown?
picks.blurb: Life comes at you fast. BYU and Texas Tech are licking their wounds after road losses to unranked teams and the league's commissioner Brett Yormark is headed out the door . The Red Raiders ' loss at Cincinnati stirred up a hornet's nest after Texas Tech billionaire booster Cody Campbell took to social media , saying: "There is no excuse or reason to lose a game like this. We have to be better." He stayed on social media throughout the week, dispelling any notion Tech coach Joey McGuire was under any sort of heat : "Joey McGuire is a perfect fit for our program, everybody, with an opinion that matters, loves him. He isn’t going anywhere." While the Red Raiders were feeling the burn of defeat, Wildcats fans were enjoying the burn of tequila. Arizona coach Brent Brennan ran up a $2,000 bar tab buying tequila shots for fans after the Wildcats' 39-3 homecoming win over Iowa State last Saturday. "I think it's important that if you want people to show up for you, you've got to show up for them and it was just an easy way for me to pop in there with all of our alumni in town and everybody for Homecoming and the excitement of the game to just go in there and say hello and get out," Brennan said. "I was there for five minutes and it was an expensive five minutes, but it was good five minutes." Just trying to invest in our fans and just let them know how much we appreciate them as a football team." Texas Tech (6-1, 3-1) fell from No. 5 in the US LBM Coaches poll to No. 14, while the Wildcats (6-1, 3-1) enter the Coaches Poll at No. 21 after five straight wins. Saturday's game has the potential to be a Big 12 championship game eliminator. So who wins? Here's what you need to know for one of Week 9's marquee games , including predictions from USA TODAY Sports reporters and beat writers from the Lubbock Avalanche-Journal , Arizona Republic and Arizona Daily Star , part of the USA TODAY Network. On a potential game-tying drive late in the fourth quarter, Noah Fifita was hit on a rollout, causing the ball to pop up and get intercepted. Fifita threw two interceptions in the second half. Will Hammond and Texas Tech bounce back. — Jeremy Cluff, Arizona Republic Texas Tech-Arizona football injury report Who will start at QB for Texas Tech: Will Hammond or Thomas Castellanos? Texas Tech spent big in the offseason and expected Brendan Sorsby to lead its offense this year. But Sorsby's gambling addiction and subsequent drama that came with it, forced the Red Raiders to lean on Will Hammond under center. The junior hasn't been great this season, with the same amount of touchdowns as interceptions (six). Florida State transfer Thomas Castellanos was brought in as a backup option, and has played sparingly, but he "will receive an uptick in snaps" on Saturday, per ESPN's Pete Thamel . Castellanos has 6,494 career passing yards over stops at UCF, Boston College, FSU and now Texas Tech. A willing runner (2,049 career rushing yards), Castellanos would give Texas Tech's offense an added dimension Is Texas Tech favored vs Arizona? away.blurb: Arizona was already dealing with injuries at wide receiver. Top receiver Tré Spivey had been ruled out for the season with a broken foot. Richardson and Hunter had also missed time earlier in the season but were available against Texas Tech. Mosley's departure further affected Arizona's wide receiver depth. Mosley's status remained uncertain following the game, as Arizona had not announced an official diagnosis or a timetable for his return after the initial evaluation. Johnson-Imagn Images The injury occurred on a third-and-18 play when quarterback Noah Fifita completed a short pass to Mosley. Medical staff quickly approached him to assess the injury. Mosley received treatment on the field before a cast was placed on his leg. The Texas Tech crowd also applauded as Mosley was taken off the field. Mosley is a freshman wide receiver who joined Arizona's 2026 recruiting class as a four-star prospect. The 6-foot-3, 197-pound receiver is from Brentwood, California, and attended Pittsburg High School. During his senior season, he recorded 82 receptions for 1,302 yards and 14 touchdowns. He wears No. 2 for the Wildcats. Against Texas Tech, Mosley recorded one reception for eight yards before leaving with the injury.

Mosley Carted Off With Leg Injury vs. Texas Tech Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today Arizona wide receiver R.J. Mosley was carted off the field with a lower-body injury during the third quarter of Saturday's game against Texas Tech. ESPN reported later in the game that Mosley would remain on the Texas Tech campus in Lubbock, where he was undergoing X-rays for what Arizona was describing as a “lower-body injury.” The injury occurred with approximately 1:27 remaining in the third quarter and Texas Tech leading Arizona 24-23 . Mosley went down after being tackled and immediately grabbed at his left knee as Arizona's medical staff rushed onto the field to evaluate him. The situation quickly appeared serious, with a cart eventually being brought onto the field and Mosley's leg being stabilized before he was taken off. ESPN's Dave Pasch told viewers that the broadcast had decided against showing additional replays because of the nature of the injury. “We're being told this is an injury we're not going to show the audience,” Pasch said during the broadcast. Arizona freshman WR R.J. Mosley took a nasty hit from a Texas Tech defender. It doesn’t look good. Prayers up 🙏 pic.twitter.com/o6CIWE5O6x R.J. Mosley Undergoing X-Rays After Injury Mosley will remain in Lubbock for further evaluation as Arizona awaits more information on the extent of the injury. The freshman wide receiver entered Saturday having caught six passes for 99 yards in four games this season, averaging 16.5 yards per reception. He had yet to record a touchdown. Mosley was coming off his longest reception of the season, a 30-yard catch in Arizona's 39-3 victory over Iowa State last week. His injury came during a critical stretch of Saturday's ranked Big 12 matchup, with the Wildcats and Red Raiders separated by just one point late in the third quarter. Mosley Carted Off After Devastating Injury Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Unfortunately for No. 22 Arizona, freshman wideout R.J. Mosley suffered a season-ending injury this Saturday against No. 13 Texas Tech. Mosley, a former four-star recruit from Pittsburgh High School, came into this Saturday's game with six catches for 99 yards on the season. During the third quarter of this afternoon's showdown, he tried to make a play for the Wildcats on an eight-yard reception. As Mosley was trying to turn upfield, a Texas Tech defender hit him right in his left knee. The Arizona wideout immediately knew something was wrong once he hit the turf. Arizona's players were understandably devastated by Mosley's injury. Some even stood there in disbelief as he was receiving medical assistance. ESPN made the classy decision to not show any replays of Mosley's injury. "We're being told this is an injury we're not going to show the audience," said ESPN announcer Dave Pasch. home.headline: WVU Injury Update: S Matt Sieg, WR Armoni Weaver-Bomar Trending to Play at Texas Tech
home.blurb: We will likely see the return of wide receiver Armoni Weaver-Bomar, and defensive lineman Corey McIntyre Jr. and cornerback Jason Chambers are not listed on the team's first availability report of the week, signaling they are on track to play this weekend against Texas Tech. Freshman safety Matt Sieg left the game against TCU a couple of weeks ago and did not return. Quite frankly, I wasn't sure that he'd be able to go for this one, considering he had his arm in a sling following that injury. The fact that it wasn't a serious ordeal is great news for the defense, but especially for him, who needs these last four games to continue to grow and develop. Mosley was taken off on a cart with an apparently serious injury to his left leg late in the third quarter of the No. 22 Wildcats' 34-26 loss at No. 13 Texas Tech on Saturday. Mosley caught a pass underneath on third-and-18 and went down short of the first down after a hit from Texas Tech cornerback Amier Boyd. Mosley reached toward his left knee as he was sitting before lying down. Arizona officials said after the game that Mosley was taken to an area hospital for further evaluation of a lower leg injury. They provided no further details. ESPN chose not to show a replay of the hit that led to the injury. Mosley's leg was in a cast when he was put onto the cart. Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita prayed as Mosley received medical attention, and his teammates surrounded him while the crowd cheered as he was driven off the field. The Wildcats were already without top receiver Tré Spivey, whose season was cut short by a broken foot. Giovanni Richardson and Chris Hunter also have missed time but were playing against the Red Raiders. There's no time to sulk over losses or complain about things not working out. Another week presents another tough test and an opportunity to right the ship. The Iowa Hawkeyes are back in action against the Wisconsin Badgers for the Battle of the Heartland, so let's dig in. Iowa lost its last outing to Minnesota in one of the sloppiest games the Hawkeyes have played under Kirk Ferentz in years. Wisconsin, on the other hand, comes to Kinnick Stadium fresh off a very strong showing in a win against USC. Iowa vs Wisconsin betting odds, spread, total Spread: Iowa -3.5 (-105), Wisconsin +3.5 (-115) Money Line: Iowa -170, Wisconsin +142 Total: Over 36.5 (-112), Under 36.5 (-108) Odds are courtesy of DraftKings Iowa opened as 4.5-point favorites, so there has been some slight movement toward Wisconsin, but nothing drastic in the overall feel of Iowa being the home favorite this week. The same can't be said for the total. The total has dropped three points to 36.5, a number fitting for this matchup. How to watch Iowa vs Wisconsin, time, TV channel, streaming Time: 11 a.m. CT Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa TV Channel: FS1 Streaming: FOX Sports App Iowa is getting the primetime coverage from FOX on this one. The Hawkeyes and Badgers get the FOX Big Noon Kickoff, which means all of the pomp and circumstance is coming to Iowa City. Expect Kinnick Stadium to be charged up for this Big Ten rivalry. Riley Donald's Iowa vs Wisconsin Prediction Prediction: Iowa 17, Wisconsin 13 I have no reason to believe we are going to see offensive fireworks in this game. Iowa knows the advantage its defense has over Wisconsin's offense and vice versa. These offenses are going to come out cautiously, not looking to make the big turnover that puts them behind. It's a classic Iowa game, really. Iowa is going to turn this to its defense, let the punt unit do its job of pinning Wisconsin deep, and find just enough juice via one or two big plays or short fields set up by winning the turnover battle. More than anything, Iowa is simply elite after a loss under Kirk Ferentz. This game has all the makings of an inspired performance from the Hawkeyes after doing everything wrong last week. Iowa gets back on track with a gritty, old-school Big Ten rivalry win. Iowa uses all of its usual tricks of suffocating the offense, doing the little things right, and making life hard on Wisconsin. It's Iowa's Halloween tricks that are scary no matter how many times it's done. Consensus line based on BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, and FanDuel. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Iowa Football vs. Wisconsin in the Battle for the Heartland
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Iowa Football vs. Wisconsin in the Battle for the Heartland Skip to main content SI.COM SPRING SPORTS HAWKEYENATION SI.COM HAWKEYES FB SI.COM HAWKEYES BB BASKETBALL BASKETBALL NEWS MEN'S SCHEDULE MEN'S RANKINGS FOOTBALL NEWS While the Floyd of Rosedale slipped out of the Iowa Hawkeyes ' grasp, another trophy is on the line this week when the Wisconsin Badgers come to Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa. The Battle for the Heartland trophy is going to be up for grabs. Iowa has dominated the Badgers for the last two seasons in two blowout wins, but this year looks like it will be a different type of game. These teams mirror each other quite well. Both play good defense, want to run the ball, and are winning games. It figures to be a four-quarter battle in this rivalry. Iowa holds Wisconsin under 150 yards passing This is a day when Iowa's secondary can shine, as we have seen in so many previous seasons. The group looks strong, led by Zach Lutmer. Outside, Jaylen Watson and Deshaun Lee are playing at a really high level, while Xavier Styles is growing each week at safety. Phil Parker is going to have Iowa containing Colton Joseph in the pocket, forcing him to beat Iowa with his arm. If Iowa can corral him and make him make tight-window throws all game, it's going to be a long day of incompletions and potentially some turnovers. DJ Vonnahme leads Iowa's passing game My gut tells me that Iowa's offense is going to have a very "2024" feel to it, like it did with Kaleb Johnson and all of the under-center zone runs. This is where DJ Vonnahme can feast. He can be the easy, big target for Hank Brown off of heavy play-action when the defense starts to flow. Iowa should look to Vonnahme early and often to get him the ball and set him up to run after the catch. When found in passing situations, I really like DJ Vonnahme down the seam. He can run and carry this route, plus he has the feel to find green grass between the linebackers and safeties. Iowa averages more yards per rush than Wisconsin Hear me out for one second - neither run game is going to be overly pretty in this game. Just prepare yourselves for that. These defenses are going to commit so many resources to stopping the run that even if responsibilities are messed up, there will be backup on standby to clean up the mess. I think Iowa's defense is going to eliminate much of the success for Wisconsin by containing Colton Joseph, which is a specialty of Phil Parker, and therefore force the backs to make something happen. Iowa can stop the run in its base defense, which it should be in for most of this game. Offensively, it won't be pretty for Iowa, but I think the Hawkeyes have a spirited run game that converts some ugly short-yardage plays and stays patient enough to get a few chunks from the running back room. It will take time, but Iowa's run game gets going just enough in this one. They're playing Iowa . Enough said. Forget the Big Ten race and the postseason implications. Forget the fact that Wisconsin has a chance to build on a tremendous win over then-No. 16 USC last week. Even forget the fact that the Badgers have lost four straight in this series. When Wisconsin plays Iowa, it's a battle between two like-minded programs. Two teams that want nothing more than to impose their will on opponents via a punishing ground game and stout, tenacious defense. This is the game, year in and year out, that provides the litmus test for the Badgers. Just how physical, how tough are they? How badly do they want it? Both have struggled at various points throughout the season, and both struggled last week at Minnesota. Now, they get an even tougher test with this Badgers defense. But more specifically, I predict Wisconsin will sack Iowa three or more times. The Hawkeyes have been very strong in pass protection with just six sacks allowed all season, and they haven't let a team sack them more than twice in a game. I see that changing Saturday afternoon. Iowa's right tackle, Jack Dotzler, has been very good at times this fall. But he's also surrendered 12 pressures and two sacks, and now he has to line up against Sebastian Cheeks, who leads the Power Four in pressures with 35 and who just racked up 2.5 sacks last week against USC. Wisconsin's pass rush showed that it could both create pressure with four-man (and sometimes even three-man) fronts, while defensive coordinator Mike Tressel also displayed an ability to scheme up pressure against a complex and high-flying Trojans offense. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Brad Schultz · Roundtable Sports Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:03 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kirk Ferentz's perspective of the Iowa-Wisconsin rivalry When Iowa football fans glanced at the 2026 schedule in the summer, one of the games that they chalked up as likely wins was a Halloween contest against rival Wisconsin. And it made perfect sense back then. The Badger program was seemingly going nowhere under head coach Luke Fickell, and many people believed 2026 would be Fickell's final season before the school would cut ties with him. But flash-forward to Halloween, and Iowa and Wisconsin enter this matchup in completely different directions. The Hawkeyes are desperate for a bounce-back win after an ugly loss at Minnesota last weekend, while the Badgers could vault themselves into College Football Playoff contention with a victory (just check their schedule after the Iowa game). Every Iowa-Wisconsin game always seems to provide something unusual, so one can only imagine what will happen on Saturday. Here's my prediction for the matchup. Matchup: No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers (5-2, 3-1) @ Iowa Hawkeyes (5-2, 2-2) Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa Scheduled game time: Oct. 31 at 11:10 a.m. Weather: 63 degrees Announcers: Gus Johnson (play-by-play), Joel Klatt (analyst), Jenny Taft (sideline) Radio: Hawkeye Radio Network (Gary Dolphin, Pat Angerer) Student Radio: KRUI (Collin Carrithers, Luke Jorden) I'm very surprised that Wisconsin is a competitive team at this point, but Iowa Everywhere's Chris Hassel said it best on Wednesday - the Badgers know their identity by now and the Hawkeyes don't. Iowa essentially using a roulette wheel to determine its starting quarterback each week has clearly caused this offense to be inconsistent week in and week out. Though Wisconsin hasn't received great quarterback play from Old Dominion transfer Colton Joseph, it has relied on a good run game and excellent defense to win football games. Sticking to that strategy has worked well for the Badgers. All you have to do to figure that out is go back and watch their last game against USC. Wisconsin dominated both lines of scrimmage en route to a 24-7 victory last weekend and you better believe they'll try and do the same thing to Iowa. But can the Badgers actually come to Kinnick Stadium and pull this one out? The momentum is definitely on Wisconsin's side of the ball, but if there's one edge Iowa has, it's the fact that it's playing at Kinnick Stadium. The Badgers haven't won in Iowa City since 2018, with the Hawkeyes winning the last three games in Kinnick by a combined score of 94-27. I don't expect a lot of points to be scored in this one (stay tuned for my betting prediction later today), but if there's one thing I know about Kirk Ferentz, it's his ability to win these Big Ten grinders. He's going to try and flip the calendar back to 2023 and win this game with complimentary football. That wouldn't be a good strategy on the road, but I think this defense will feed off the home crowd and give their offense enough short fields to secure a narrow victory. The Hawkeyes take down Wisconsin for the sixth time in seven games. Prediction: Iowa 16, Wisconsin 13

Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images (Matt Krohn, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 1 / 21 Iowa football releases Week 9 depth chart vs. Wisconsin Iowa football releases Week 9 depth chart vs. Wisconsin Iowa football vs. Minnesota: Best photos from Week 8 'Not good enough': Kirk Ferentz laments Iowa's QB play vs. Minnesota CBS shares Iowa football bowl projection after Minnesota loss Iowa football plummets in updated US LBM Coaches Poll rankings Iowa football falls out of latest AP Top 25 poll rankings Josh Helmer: Iowa has owned this series of late, winning each of the past four and outscoring the Badgers during that stretch, 118-26. I just don't see Saturday playing out in a similar, lopsided fashion. This will be your typical grind-it-out, lean on the defense and special teams, field position battle. Two great defenses take the field in this contest: Wisconsin and Iowa rank 13th and 14th nationally in total defense. The Hawkeyes are No. 8 in scoring defense (14.3 points per game), while the Badgers rank No. 12 (15.3 points per game). Iowa's quarterback questions have reemerged after Jeremy Hecklinski was benched last week in favor of former starter Hank Brown. There's run game concerns for Iowa, too. Leading rusher Kamari Moulton is out for the remainder of the season, and this Hawkeye offense hasn't generated much of anything on the ground against power foes outside of its win at Washington . Iowa wins, but it's on the backs of the Hawkeyes' defense and special teams. Prediction: Iowa 17, Wisconsin 13 Scout Springgate: In a sport that has already delivered incredible moments so far this year, the battle for the Heartland Trophy between Iowa and Wisconsin has suddenly become extremely important for both sides. For Iowa, it's a must-win game after an abysmal offensive showing at Minnesota last week. Looking ahead, Iowa travels to a rowdy Ryan Field to face a red-hot Northwestern program next week and needs this win to avoid heading there on a two-game losing streak and with its CFP hopes completely dashed. In what should be a low-scoring defensive battle, it will come down to whether Iowa can capitalize on their scoring opportunities and sustain enough drives where they don't hang their defense out to dry. With the game in front of a sold-out Kinnick Stadium, I feel confident Iowa can pull out a victory over Wisconsin by making critical defensive plays and having the offense do just enough to win. However, I don't foresee the Hawkeyes necessarily answering the litany of questions and concerns on offense with their performance. Prediction: Iowa 16, Wisconsin 10 Zach Hiney: It's funny how quickly things can change in sports. Just one week ago, Iowa was 5-1, and many thought they had a shot at making the College Football Playoff. Now, the general mood within the fanbase is very negative following a poor showing in a loss to Minnesota. Playoff hopes are dashed, and questions at quarterback have popped back up. In addition to their own internal issues, the Hawkeyes will also have to contend with a hot Wisconsin team on Saturday. The Badgers are coming off a big home win over USC and are playing their best football in years. New quarterback Colton Joseph didn't do much against the Trojans, but has largely been a positive this season. He has 15 total touchdowns and is a dangerous dual-threat option. Wisconsin's defense has been stellar recently, giving up only 27 total points in their last three games. That includes a dominant performance against USC, where they held the high-powered Trojans to just seven points. Now they'll get to play an Iowa offense in complete disarray. Hank Brown will start at quarterback, but his effectiveness will be the big question. He'll have to operate without leading rusher Kamari Moulton, who's out for the season with an injury. I don't have a lot of confidence in Iowa's offense at the moment. The Moulton injury is a big blow. I envision that unit having some problems on Saturday. But I do have a lot of confidence in Phil Parker's defense. Joseph is a fine quarterback, but he's the kind of guy Iowa has made its hay against during Parker's tenure. I expect the Hawkeyes' defense to turn in another strong performance. Throw in the fact that this game is at Kinnick Stadium, and I feel decent about Iowa's chances. The Hawkeyes win, but don't answer many of the questions about their offense in the process. And the Heartland Trophy won't be the only thing on the line. For the visiting Badgers , they're looking to prove that last week's win over USC wasn't a fluke. Luke Fickell's team is off to a strong 5-2 start and playing some good football on both sides of the ball. This is the final big test for Wisconsin. After this game, the last four opponents on their schedule have a combined record of 12-16 this season. A win here would vault Wisconsin into College Football Playoff talks. For the Hawkeyes , this game is all about bouncing back. They played a sloppy game last weekend and picked up a deserved loss to Minnesota in the process. There are questions at quarterback, Kamari Moulton is done for the year, and the fanbase is uneasy about how the offense is going to perform on a week-to-week basis. This game is an opportunity to right the ship while picking up a win over a good team in the process. With so much on the line for both teams, who do the experts have winning? Here are the experts' predictions for Iowa vs. Wisconsin. Iowa vs. Wisconsin expert predictions Bleacher Report : Iowa 20, Wisconsin 13. David Kenyon of Bleacher Report picked the Hawkeyes in a close one. He explained his reasoning: "First to 20? Expect two stout defenses and a barrage of punts in this rivalry tilt," Kenyon said. "As USC just learned, Wisconsin is fully capable of winning on the strength of takeaways and favorable field position. Iowa also committed four turnovers in its recent loss at Minnesota. At home, though, Iowa holds a slight edge." College Football News : Iowa 16, Wisconsin 13. Pete Fiutak of College Football News is rolling with Iowa in a low-scoring affair. He talked more about the game and his pick: "Iowa has been held to under 100 rushing yards four times," Fiutak said. "The losses to Ohio State and Minnesota, the 16-13 win over Iowa State, and the minor-miracle 20-19 win at Michigan. The Iowa running game has been feast-or-famine – totally dominating in the wins over everyone but Michigan. It's not going to dominate against this Badger defense, but … Wisconsin isn't completing passes. This will be about field position, mistakes, and one big play in a tough dogfight. Like the loss at UCLA, the Badgers will play well, and it won't be enough on the road." Sports Illustrated : Iain MacMillan of Sports Illustrated picked Iowa to protect Kinnick Stadium and win this game. He explained why: Wisconsin has to be able to run the ball to be an effective offense," MacMillan said. "Unfortunately, Iowa has one of the best run defenses in the nation, ranking second in opponent EPA per rush and seventh in opponent rush success rate. Not being able to run the ball means the Hawkeyes are going to have an advantage in this game. The Wisconsin defense is good, but they're a full step below the Hawkeyes' defense." away.headline: 5 key numbers from Iowa football's 30-0 win over Wisconsin
away.blurb: The Hawkeyes delivered, with a 30-0 win over the Badgers at Kinnick Stadium on Oct. 31. Quarterback Hank Brown had a great day slinging the ball and the Iowa defense was lights-out the entire afternoon. In the first half, Brown had 190 passing yards, completed 16 out of 18 passes and had two touchdowns. By the end of the game, he finished with 222 yards, with 20 completions on 24 attempts for an 83% completion percentage. Buhr drilled all his attempts on the day, three field goals and three PATs. The first was from 24 yards out on the first drive of the game. The second was from 28 yards out at the end of the second quarter. The defense dominated, only allowing Wisconsin to have nine first downs all game, compared to Iowa's 20. The Badgers only converted on 3-out-of-12 third downs. Football Men's Hoops Women's Hoops Wrestling IOWA WOMEN'S BASKETBALL 5 key numbers from Iowa football's 30-0 win over Wisconsin Mackenzie Meaney Des Moines Register Updated Oct. 31, 2026, 4:06 p.m. CT The Iowa Hawkeyes defeated the Wisconsin Badgers 30-0 in a bounce-back victory. Quarterback Hank Brown completed 83% of his passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns. DJ Vonnahme scored two touchdowns, one receiving and one rushing. IOWA CITY — Iowa football players spoke at their weekly media availability ahead of Saturday's Wisconsin game, saying they wanted to show the world a bounce-back game after a disappointing 13-10 loss to Minnesota. Here are five key numbers that tell the story of Iowa's win. 83: Hank Brown's completion percentage Brown was named the starter by head coach Kirk Ferentz on Tuesday and in his first start since the loss to Ohio State, Brown played his best game of his season so far. Brown looked really calm and collected during the trophy game for Iowa. Diaz was one of many receivers with a solid game, with four catches for 75 yards and a touchdown. It was his first game with a score since the Week 1 win over Northern Illinois. The star transfer has delivered in key moments this season, like on the drives that helped the Hawkeyes beat Iowa State and Michigan, or the grab he had to help the scoring drive against Minnesota. Diaz also showed his versatility in the game when Tim Lester dialed up a rushing play, which went for 20 yards and nearly ended in the end zone. 2: DJ Vonnahme's total touchdowns Vonnahme caught the first touchdown of the game in the first quarter off a 4-yard pass and later rushed for a 2-yard score. That marked his first career rushing touchdown. In total, Vonnahme finished with five catches for 54 yards in the air, and two rushes for 10 yards. home.headline: Iowa Football Injury Update: Hawkeyes Banged Up, Northwestern Face Huge Question Mark
home.blurb: Two of Iowa's starting defensive backs are nursing some sort of injury and are listed as questionable heading into this weekend's contest against Northwestern. Starting cornerback Jaylen Watson and the do-it-all safety Zach Lutmer are each trying to get ready to go on Saturday. Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles is questionable The most shocking name on the availability report is Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles. He is currently listed as questionable for the game this weekend, which completely changes the complexion of things if he isn't ready to go. He didn't exit Northwestern's last game against Oregon early with an injury, but he did go just 5-for-14 in the second half. Could that have been injury-related, or the Ducks' defense figuring out Northwestern a bit more as the game went on? My gut tells me Chiles is going this weekend, and in all honesty, is probably closer to 100% healthy than he is questionable for being able to play. One thing to watch, depending on what the injury is, could be his impact on the ground. You can tell that college football has hit the month of November. Not only are the temperatures about to begin dropping across Big Ten country, but the injury reports are starting to grow longer and longer each weekend for everyone in the conference. The Iowa Hawkeyes and Northwestern Wildcats have put together quite a lengthy availability report that features a total of 29 players listed on the report in some capacity heading into the weekend. Both teams see key players on the report, too, that raise some concerns. Iowa is thin on the offensive line After holding up for most of the year across the front, Iowa's offensive line is starting to see its depth go away in a hurry. Starting center Cael Winter is going to miss this game, along with key depth pieces Lucas Allgeyer, Trent Wilson, and Cannon Leonard. Iowa is paper-thin across the offensive line now. Fortunately, four of the five starters remain in the lineup, with Michael Myslinski slotting in at the starting center position in place of Cael Winter. Question marks in Iowa's secondary My intuition tells me Iowa is likely to have both of them, as neither seemed horribly banged up after the Wisconsin contest, but only time will tell, along with a pregame workout on the field, as to whether one or both of Watson and Lutmer are good to go. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Ole Miss against Auburn Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Today at 11:45 a.m. CT, the No. 12 Ole Miss Rebels play the Auburn Tigers at home . Both teams are looking to bounce back following losses. Auburn lost 38-17 last Saturday to the No. 15 LSU Tigers. Ole Miss lost 34-27 to the No. 11 Texas Longhorns last Saturday. Both teams were coming off victories over ranked opponents the week before their losses and are looking to reignite the momentum they had prior to last week's losses. With the stage set, let's get into my three bold predictions for the game. 1. Trinidad Chambliss Has No Turnovers Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss throws a pass during the first quarter against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has been very efficient this season. However, there is one lingering issue standing out on his stat sheet: he keeps turning the ball over. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has been very efficient this season. However, there is one lingering issue standing out on his stat sheet: he keeps turning the ball over. Chambliss has thrown an interception in all but two games this season. He's also fumbled four times, although only two led to turnovers. Texas was the worst game so far this season for interceptions, as he threw three of them, although the last was on a Hail Mary as time expired. Chambliss has been great aside from the turnovers, as he's scored 22 touchdowns and has over 2,000 combined yards. However, the Rebels need to go on a winning streak to make the College Football Playoff, and Chambliss' turnover issues will stop that from happening if they are not improved immediately. I expect that improvement to start against Auburn. 2. Backup Running Backs Show Flashes Mississippi Rebels running back Makhi Frazier carries the ball during the second half against the Missouri Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A major concern heading into this matchup, and potentially the rest of the season, is who can step up for Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy now that he's missing time with a dislocated shoulder . Running backs Makhi Frazier , JT Lindsey and Shekai Mills-Knight have been mentioned as players with opportunities to fill Lacy's role in the offense. I expect Ole Miss to utilize a rotation of rushers against Auburn, which likely lowers the ceiling of any running back's individual performance. However, that doesn't mean that one or more of them won't impress on Saturday. I expect a rushing touchdown or two from the committee and an impressive yards per carry average, even if it's unlikely for any of them to break the 100-yard rushing mark. 3. It's no exaggeration to say he's been nearly the entire offense. It's no exaggeration to say he's been nearly the entire offense. However, against LSU last week, he just couldn't get anything going. He finished the game with 160 passing yards for no passing touchdowns, as well as 20 rushing yards on 19 rushes for one touchdown. While Ole Miss' defense hasn't been fantastic this season at defending mobile quarterbacks, I expect the Rebels' defense to return to the level they played at against Vanderbilt and No. 23 Missouri. In those two games, the opposing teams scored just 20 combined points against Ole Miss. The performance against Texas wasn't all bad for the defense, but heading into the final stretch of the season, where things have to go right for the Rebels, I think the defense makes its presence felt for the whole game instead of just in moments. Both teams are entering Week 9 coming off losses, but it's the Rebels that are playing with pressure for their playoff lives moving forward. Though Auburn is sitting at 4-3 (2-3) through what's been an up and down season up to this point, the Tigers are no slouch. Just two weeks ago Auburn went into Athens and pulled out a last-second win over Georgia. Kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 11:45 a.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss will enter game day as a double-digit home favorite. Ahead of the Rebels' latest conference matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Oct 24, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) warms up before the game against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Not that it matters by any means, but aside from its impressive road win against Georgia two weeks ago, nothing particularly jumps off the page to me about Alex Golesh's first team at Auburn. That's not to say Golesh isn't the right fit for the job either. He has the Tigers sitting above .500 and is working through his first season as a head coach at a Power Four program. As it pertains to the game itself, I expect Ole Miss to maintain its home win streak that dates back to September of the 2024 season. This certainly should be a focused group after picking up its second loss in Texas last weekend and they can't afford to overlook Auburn even though Georgia is around the corner. Controlling their playoff destiny is on thin ice. Trinidad Chambliss could use a bounce back game after not looking like himself the past two weeks. Considering Auburn's weaker pass defense through its secondary, I believe Chambliss does what he desperately needs to do and may even incorporate his legs more than usual. Ole Miss needs to prove it can find a faster start on the offensive side of the ball as a whole. Defensively, Ole Miss should match up well against an offense that has already surrendered 29 sacks (4.3 per game) if the unit can contain Byrum Brown. The Tigers' quarterback leads the team in rushing yards, but still looks like a signal-caller in his first season in the SEC. Ole Miss 31, Auburn 17 While Auburn is more than capable of pulling off the upset, just look at its victory over No. 3 Georgia in Athens, I don't see it happening this Saturday. Against Texas, the Ole Miss offense did everything it could to let Texas pull away. However, despite struggling for most of the night, they lost the game by just seven points. The two games prior to Texas, Ole Miss won by blowing out its opponents. With the Rebels' back against the wall and needing to go on a win streak if they want to make the College Football Playoff, I think they win easily against Auburn and carry some nice momentum into their matchup against the Georgia Bulldogs next Saturday night. Ole Miss 34, Auburn 17 Cooper Ferguson Alex Golesh will take this Auburn team to greener pastures than Hugh Freeze ever did, and I think that in the alternate universe where Golesh came to Auburn, things worked out. A great coach tasked with waking a sleeping giant, I think Auburn will, in due time, become a force to be reckoned with again in the SEC. That time is not now, though. Florida and the first half against Texas need to be remembered as blips in a strong season for the Rebels in years to come. With a strong showing against Auburn this Halloween, Ole Miss will be well on its way to correcting its path. Chambliss and Co. dispatch the Tigers easily, and Ole Miss moves on to prep for Georgia. Ole Miss 49, Auburn 14 Billy Flowers Byrum Brown will be a major problem for the Ole Miss run defense, but Auburn's offensive line is horrific. I think the Tigers' only path to victory is through Brown's legs, which, frankly, will not put enough points on the board for Auburn. I think Trinidad bounces back, and Makhai Frazier has a breakout performance against the Tiger's less-than-stellar rush defense. I do think Auburn can keep the game close, thanks to their rushing attack. The Ole Miss offense is too talented, and the Tigers won't score enough to match it. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27 Zion Trammell Ole Miss is coming off a disappointing performance against Texas and really needs a solid response this week. The key to victory is to keep Byrum Brown in the pocket. The Auburn quarterback can make big plays with his legs, so limiting his mobility will be a priority. The Tigers knocked off Georgia a couple of weeks ago, but I think Pete Golding's team responds well at home. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 24 The Ole Miss Rebels face a must-win game against the Auburn Tigers. They won't disappoint. Auburn is a dangerous football team, but Ole Miss will show its talent when it needs to. Trinidad Chambliss will have a day as the defense struggles at first but settles in. The Rebels, in the end, will win this game by three-plus touchdowns. picks.blurb: ESPN predicts the winner of Saturday's game between Auburn and Ole Miss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings ESPN predicts the winner of Saturday's game between Auburn and Ole Miss Phillip Jordan, Auburn Wire · Auburn Wire Thu, October 29, 2026 at 7:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Auburn Tigers are looking to rebound after playing poorly in a 38-17 home loss to LSU. Who does ESPN have winning when Auburn travels to Ole Miss on Saturday? According to the ESPN Matchup Predictor , Auburn has a 25.1% chance of picking up a victory at Ole Miss. The Tigers have not lost back-to-back games this season and will be looking to avoid that in Oxford, Mississippi, on Saturday. It will be a tall task for Auburn to come away with a win over the Rebels, who are coming off a narrow defeat last week at the hands of the Texas Longhorns . Ole Miss almost made a huge comeback after trailing Texas 24-3 at halftime. Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss could not find the end zone as time expired, and Ole Miss lost 34-27. At 5-2, Ole Miss can not afford another loss if they want to make the College Football Playoff. This will be the first meeting between the two schools since the 2023 season , when Ole Miss defeated Auburn in the first year of the Hugh Freeze era. These two programs met each year when they were both part of the SEC West division. Auburn leads the all-time series 35-12, but Ole Miss has won the last two meetings. In the final five games of the season, Auburn should be able to snap their streak of five consecutive losing seasons. With four wins, Auburn should be able to get three more victories with games against Arkansas, Mississippi State, and Samford. A matchup that could help Auburn pull off an upset victory over Ole Miss is in the run game. The Rebels are at the bottom of the SEC, giving up 161.1 yards per game on the ground. Saturday could be an opportunity for Byrum Brown and the Auburn running backs to have a big game. picks.headline: Final score predictions for Ole Miss vs. Auburn: Can the Rebels bounce back and save their College Football Playoff hopes?
picks.blurb: Final score predictions for Ole Miss vs. Auburn: Can the Rebels bounce back and save their College Football Playoff hopes? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Final Score predictions for Ole Miss Rebels and Auburn Tigers Scott Wachter-Imagn Images and John Reed-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness · AtoZ Sports Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:54 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Ole Miss Rebels are in a position to bounce back against an Auburn team that looked bad last week. The Ole Miss Rebels lost to the Texas Longhorns last week. The loss does not help their College Football Playoff chances at all. In fact, they now have a 44% chance of making the postseason. A win over the Auburn Tigers on Saturday would move that to 53%, according to A to Z's Simulator. As for Auburn, they have a 1% chance to make it . And, with a win over Ole Miss, that jumps to just 7%. They then have to play Alabama in Week 13, too. This could be a great game with real implications. So, our experts broke it all down. Final Score Predictions for Ole Miss vs. Auburn Ole Miss 34, Auburn 16: Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame Ole Miss takes care of business against Auburn with a 34-16 win, thanks largely to a monster performance from quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. With Kewan Lacy sidelined, the Rebels needed someone to step up offensively, and Chambliss delivered. He makes plays with both his arm and his legs, keeping Auburn's defense on its heels and helping Ole Miss avoid a major drop-off without one of its key offensive weapons. The Rebels find success through the air and do enough on the ground to keep the offense balanced, putting Auburn in a difficult spot for most of the afternoon. Auburn's offensive struggles continue as the Tigers struggle to put together consistent drives against an Ole Miss defense that takes advantage of their mistakes. The Tigers may find a few scoring chances, but they lack the consistency to make this a competitive second half. As Auburn's offense stalls, Chambliss and the Rebels capitalize, gradually building a comfortable lead and putting the game out of reach. Ole Miss leaves with a 34-16 win, and Chambliss proves he can carry a significant portion of the offensive load even without Lacy in the lineup. Ole Miss 35, Auburn 20: Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama After a big win over Georgia a couple of weeks ago, the Tigers came back to Earth against LSU last weekend, and things won't get any easier against Ole Miss this week. The Rebels will look to bounce back after a loss to the Longhorns, with their playoff lives on the line. I don't know how Auburn plans to contain Trinidad Chambliss, but he'll be back and hungry to make plays after a down performance against Texas. An Auburn defense that has struggled for much of the season may be the perfect scenario for this team and Trinidad Chambliss. Give me Ole Miss by a wide margin. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 24: Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida I was high on Auburn after their upset win over Georgia and genuinely thought they'd beat the LSU Tigers. Well, they instead got smoked and got exposed as not ready to compete. Ole Miss is now on life support in the playoff race, having lost to Florida and Texas, two other SEC foes who also have two losses. Trinidad Chambliss was very inconsistent against the Longhorns and will use this as a get-right game for the stretch run. Ole Miss 31, Auburn 23: Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee In a game the Rebels cannot afford to lose to stay in the playoff picture, it starts with a bit of a scare. Byrum Brown and the Tigers get off to another strong road start, building an early lead and leaning on the ground game to shorten the game and keep Trinidad Chambliss on the sideline longer than Rebel fans want. But the Rebels get things going quickly in the second half. As Sam Leavitt and the Tigers did from the jump last week against Auburn, Chambliss and his targets get in rhythm and push ahead in the third quarter. Auburn keeps it interesting until the end, but they can't pull off the big road upset for the second time in as many tries. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Auburn football gets much-needed boost with positive injury report
away.blurb: The Tigers record took a beating from the game, but so did its secondary, which suffered from injuries throughout the matchup. Safety Sylvester Smith-Reed, nickel AnQuon "Newboy" Fegans and cornerback Andre Jordan Jr. were all sideline throughout various points of Saturday's game, but according to head coach Alex Golesh, all three players were out on the field practicing on Monday. Starting corner Jordan exited the game after just three plays and did not return to the game, and Fegans seemed to be dealing with a leg injury before heading out of the game in the second quarter. Smith-Reed left the game after a pass breakup in the second half. At the tail end of the season, in the midst of the brutal play in the SEC, Golesh know that depth is an important factor in finishing strong. Also with the potential to return to action this weekend is sophomore wide receiver Jeremiah Koger. Golesh said he was close to be able to play against Ole Miss but was ultimately ruled out, and the Tigers hope to have him back against Arkansas. The Tigers return home this weekend and host the Arkansas Razorbacks for an 11:45 a.m. kickoff from Jordan-Hare Stadium. Auburn football gets much-needed boost with positive injury report Skip to main content About It was a tough weekend for the Auburn football team as they suffered another conference loss, falling 45-15 against Pete Golding and the Ole Miss Rebels in Oxford. ""You have to have a level of depth (for) a gauntlet," Golesh said . "Whether Arkansas is ranked or not, that's a physical football team that's fighting their tails off, and it's going to be the same as it's been the last four weeks. That part won't change. "Depth matters. You've got to be able to count on every single guy on the roster to provide something." Although it was a positive injury report, Golesh provided no guarantees that any of the four players will be good to go this weekend. He said later in the week he would have a better idea of who would be ready to play.

away.blurb: Top Auburn WR Listed as Questionable Ahead of Ole Miss Matchup Skip to main content SI.COM Koger was listed as questionable on the Tigers’ initial injury report Thursday meaning that he has around a 50% chance to play, while offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring are listed as out. At this time, it is unclear as to why exactly Koger is listed as questionable, but it goes without saying that losing his production would be a significant blow for the Tigers, as he currently ranks third among all Tigers in total receiving yards. Koger was a four-star recruit out of St. Frances Academy in Baltimore, Maryland, when he signed with Alex Golesh and the USF Bulls, earning playing time quite early in his young career. Last season, his freshman year, Koger hauled in 38 Byrum Brown passes for 597 yards and eight touchdowns before transferring to the Plains this past offseason. If Koger is ruled out for the game against Ole Miss, the Tigers still have plenty of other talent to turn to in the interim, including fellow USF transfer receiver Christian Neptune, who completed a touchdown pass to Singleton against Georgia, as well as DeShawn Spencer, a true freshman who has hauled in 10 passes for 90 yards and two touchdowns so far this season. The Auburn Tigers are looking to rebound from a devastating loss to LSU, in which the Bayou Bengals came to town and routed the home team by 21 points, though that effort may get a little more difficult with the potential absence of one key wide receiver: Jeremiah Koger. The Maryland native was highly anticipated on the Plains and has lived up to a large part of those expectations, though he has not yet quite turned in the statistical production of the Tigers’ top two receivers, Keshaun Singleton and Chas Nimrod, both of whom are also new Auburn transfers from USF. So far this season, Koger has caught 14 passes for 230 yards, both stats ranking third on the team. Notably, however, Koger has yet to bring in a touchdown for the Tigers this year, which is quite surprising given his production at USF last season. Singleton and Nimrod have worked to make up for that, though, hauling in a combined five touchdown passes from Brown this season. They’ve also combined for 69 total receptions and 771 receiving yards, a high mark for any Auburn duo. The Tigers are scheduled to square off against Ole Miss this Saturday, October 31, at 11:45 a.m. CT, in a matchup that is scheduled to be broadcast on SEC Network. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched.” Georgia: WR Isiah Canion (lower extremity, probable), RB Chauncey Bowens (lower body, questionable), WR Thomas Blackshear (collarbone, questionable), TE Elyiss Williams (undisclosed, questionable), DT Joseph Jonah-Ajonye (undisclosed, questionable), DB Tyriq Green (leg, questionable), LB AJ Kruah (undisclosed, questionable) RB Dante Dowdell (multiple injuries including collarbone, lung and arm, out), OLB Amaris Williams (knee, out). home.headline: Ole Miss vs. Georgia injury report: Kewan Lacy out, Luke Ferrelli in
home.blurb: The first Ole Miss availability report for Georgia landed Wednesday, and like most injury reports this time of year, it came with a little bit of everything. Let's start with the good news. Linebacker Luke Ferrelli wasn't listed at all. Considering where things stood a week ago, that's a significant development. Ferrelli has been battling an ankle injury for weeks and spent all of last week on the report after aggravating it in practice. He started against Auburn but was limited before leaving the game early. His absence from Wednesday's report is about as positive a sign as Ole Miss could have hoped for heading into Saturday's showdown with No. 2 Georgia. Now for the bad news. Running back Kewan Lacy and safety Edwin Joseph are both out. Lacy's status was expected . Ole Miss has been preparing as if it would be without its star running back, so there were no surprises there. Joseph's designation is a little tougher to swallow. There was at least a sliver of hope he could return after missing four straight games following ankle surgery, but that won't happen this week. The rest of the report falls somewhere in the middle. Defensive lineman Kam Franklin and leading tackler Keaton Thomas were listed as questionable, while cornerback Jalyn Crawford and left tackle Terez Davis were listed as probable. None of those designations are expected to keep them off the field Saturday. For the first time in the history of the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party, Florida and Georgia will play in Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with kickoff slated this afternoon at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Bulldogs are 11.5-point favorites on Saturday, Oct. 31, and my Florida vs. Georgia prediction and college football picks expect Kirby Smart's team to take advantage of Jon Sumrall's defense in his first Cocktail Party. Who will win Florida vs Georgia: Georgia -11.5 Kirby Smart has owned the Florida vs. Georgia rivalry recently, winning eight of the last nine games. While he's just 5-4 against the spread in those games, his Bulldogs have the advantage against a sporadic Florida team. But without knowing which version of Florida we'll get, I would only take the Bulldogs up to -12.5 . Georgia's defense is far more trustworthy than Florida's, ranking 14th nationally in available yards percentage (35.7%) , 21st in defensive success rate (35.4%), and holding six of seven opponents to 20 or fewer points. With athletes like Chris Cole and Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia is well-equipped to deal with Buster Faulkner's misdirection-heavy offense. Plus, the Gators' top two QBs ( Aaron Philo , Tramell Jones Jr. ) are questionable , and while I expect them to play, it could impact their consistency. In a high-scoring game, Georgia's defense will make enough stops to cover. TOP PICK Florida vs Georgia Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 Georgia has been an Over machine this season, hitting it in six of seven games, despite its defense allowing just 15.9 points per game. I like the Over to hit at 55.5 or better for the fifth time in the last seven Cocktail Parties, especially given Faulkner's familiarity with Smart and Georgia's defense. Faulkner worked for Smart at Georgia for three years before spending the last three seasons as Georgia Tech's offensive coordinator; his offenses averaged 24.6 points and 392 yards against the Bulldogs. With one of the top running backs in the country in Jadan Baugh , who ranks top 10 in forced missed tackles (40), Florida should score 20+. Its defense will do the rest of the job for the Over. Florida has one of the worst defenses in the Power Four, r anking 125th in the country in defensive success rate (49.5%) , and it hasn't played an offense as efficient as Georgia's yet this season. Florida vs Georgia combo Some weeks Florida looks like a College Football Playoff team (against Ole Miss and Texas ), and other weeks it looks like it might not win eight games (against Missouri and South Carolina ). Which version will come to play in the World's Largest Cocktail Party? If Auburn hadn't improbably upset the Bulldogs the last time they played, they would probably be closer to 14.5-point favorites because of Florida's defensive struggles and offensive injuries. Coming out of a bye, I expect Smart to have Georgia ready to roll in a rivalry game he's dominated and to pull away in the second half against a Florida defense that ranks second-worst in havoc rate in the SEC (14.5%). Georgia -11.5 Georgia fourth quarter -2.5 Florida vs Georgia prop: Georgia team total Over 34.5 Florida's defense has been the death of it this season, allowing 34.2 points per game against SEC opponents. With Georgia averaging 33.6 points per game in SEC play, I like the Over on the Bulldogs' team total at 34.5 or better . The Gators have played four quarterbacks who rank top 50 nationally in QBR this season; in those four games, they've allowed an average of 37.5 points per game , with three of four opponents scoring 38+ points. Seven of the eight analysts who made predictions across College GameDay and SEC Nation picked the No. 3 Bulldogs to defeat No. 20 Florida at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Tim Tebow was the lone dissenting voice, backing his alma mater despite acknowledging several advantages for Georgia. The predictions come as both programs return from their bye weeks. Florida (5-2, 3-2 SEC) looks to build on its 27-24 upset victory over Texas, while Georgia (6-1, 4-1) tries to recover from a 27-24 loss to Auburn. College GameDay picks Georgia unanimously ESPN's College GameDay broadcast from Bloomington, Indiana, ahead of the Hoosiers' matchup with Minnesota. The panel unanimously selected Georgia to beat Florida, with Desmond Howard, Nick Saban, Pat McAfee, and celebrity guest picker Isiah Thomas all siding with the Bulldogs. Kirk Herbstreit did not make a prediction because he is calling the game for ABC alongside Chris Fowler. The show's fan poll also heavily favored Georgia, with 76% of respondents picking the Bulldogs. Here's how the College GameDay panel voted: Desmond Howard: Georgia Nick Saban: Georgia Pat McAfee: Georgia Isiah Thomas: Georgia Kirk Herbstreit: No pick Tim Tebow stands alone on SEC Nation The SEC Nation crew broadcast from Atlanta, where Paul Finebaum, Roman Harper and Chase Daniel all picked Georgia. Tebow was the only panelist to give Florida the nod. Finebaum expressed little uncertainty about the matchup. "Georgia is really good. Florida is a mystery," Finebaum said. "This is not a difficult pick at all. The Dogs are going to win it." Harper acknowledged that Florida has a path to victory, particularly if the Gators utilize both Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. at quarterback, but ultimately sided with Georgia because of his confidence in Kirby Smart. Tebow appeared to reach the same conclusion. He praised Smart as the nation's best coach, described Georgia as the country's most complete team and highlighted quarterback Gunner Stockton as a major advantage for the Bulldogs. However, the former Florida quarterback shifted his focus to the emotion surrounding the rivalry and the people who make college football meaningful. After reflecting on a feature about Jadan Baugh and personal connections to the game, Tebow emphatically picked Florida to pull off the upset. The Bulldogs (6-1) are looking to bounce back from a stunning 27-24 loss to Auburn, while the Gators (5-2) are hoping to build on their impressive road victory over Texas. With plenty on the line for both programs, former Georgia quarterback and current SEC Network analyst Aaron Murray has weighed in with his prediction for Saturday's showdown. During a recent episode of the Aaron Murray College Football Show , Murray broke down the matchup before ultimately picking his former team to come out on top. "The Dawgs win 35 to 27," Murray predicted. Aaron Murray Expects Gunner Stockton to Bounce Back Against Florida Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect One of Murray's biggest reasons for picking Georgia is his confidence in Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton. Stockton struggled with turnovers in Georgia's loss to Auburn, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble that helped set up the Tigers' game-winning field goal. However, Murray believes those mistakes were an exception rather than a sign of bigger problems. Murray also pointed to Florida's struggling secondary as a potential opportunity for Stockton to put together a big performance. The Gators are allowing approximately 255 passing yards per game, something Murray believes Georgia can exploit with its talented group of receivers. He also emphasized the importance of Florida winning the battle at the line of scrimmage. If the Gators cannot generate pressure on Stockton, Murray expects the Bulldogs' offense to have a productive afternoon. Georgia-Florida Matchup Carries Major SEC Playoff Implications USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Saturday's rivalry game is about much more than bragging rights. Georgia enters the weekend with a 4-1 SEC record and remains firmly in the conference championship race despite its recent setback against Auburn. Florida, meanwhile, sits at 3-2 in conference play and has little room for another loss if it hopes to remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. A Georgia victory would strengthen the Bulldogs' position in the SEC race while delivering a significant blow to Florida's postseason hopes. However, a Gators upset would create another major shakeup in an already unpredictable SEC championship race. The longtime rivals will meet at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta rather than their traditional Jacksonville location due to ongoing stadium renovations. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. away.blurb: No. 25 Florida (5-3, 3-3 SEC) listed seven players on its initial availability report before facing Oklahoma (4-4, 2-3 SEC) in Gainesville on Saturday, with wide receiver Vernell Brown III listed as doubtful, defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca , offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson ruled out for the contest. In addition, wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo are listed as questionable. Vernell Brown III – doubtful DL Jeramiah McCloud – out WR Bailey Stockton – questionable DL Emmanuel Oyebadejo – questionable McCloud is out due to a suspension, according to a program spokesperson, who provided a statement to Swamp247. The latest update for Brown III comes on the heels of Jon Sumrall stressing Monday that the sophomore pass-catcher was doing everything possible to return, having been sidelined since Sept. 26 with a grade-1 PCL strain that was re-aggravated in the build-up to Florida's 27-8 loss in Atlanta to Georgia. "So he had a little thing done this morning to address hopefully some of the issue. The thing I want to make abundantly clear here is he's trying like hell to play. And the frustrating thing for him is he looked good Monday, Tuesday. He looked good most of Wednesday – had the little setback Wednesday at practice that at the time we felt like was a little setback, and then woke up Thursday with more swelling than we anticipated - and not as much range of motion. That's why on Wednesday when he left the building, he's like, 'I feel pretty good. I feel better than I thought I would.' After he had what was what we thought a little setback," Sumrall said Monday. "So listing think probable if I'm not mistaken last Wednesday, and then he got downgraded on Thursday to questionable if I'm not mistaken because Thursday is when he woke up and the swelling was more noticeable and the range of motion had decreased. So he was not available at practice today. I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because, like I said everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." As if that didn't make it clear, Sumrall cleared up any notion the sophomore was opting out of the remainder of the regular season amid UF's 1-3 record in October following the team's impressive 4-0 start. As for Duke Clark , the sophomore running back is set to return after missing Florida's last three games after suffering a foot injury against South Carolina .
