picks.blurb: Oregon Ducks vs. Northwestern Wildcats Final Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Transfer Portal FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2024 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM DUCKS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM DUCKS BB Northwestern offensive coordinator Chip Kelly makes his return to Oregon on Saturday leading the No. 20 Wildcats into Eugene for their first ever showdown at Autzen Stadium. Kelly coached Oregon between 2009 and 2012, compiling a 46-7 record and four consecutive BCS bowl appearances. His homecoming arrives as the Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) are debuting a new play caller Jay Johnson. Jan. 3, 2013; Glendale, AZ, USA; Oregon Ducks coach Chip Kelly looks on against the Kansas State Wildcats during the Fiesta Bowl at University of Phoenix Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Kartozian-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oregon coach Dan Lanning handed the keys to the offense to Johnson after dismissing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday following the Ducks’ 21-10 loss to Illinois. Oregon coach Dan Lanning handed the keys to the offense to Johnson after dismissing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday following the Ducks’ 21-10 loss to Illinois. Northwestern (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten) brings a vaunted rushing attack under Kelly and a four-game winning streak, while Oregon breaks in a revised offense desperately in need of a spark to save what minimal chances the Ducks have left of winning the Big Ten. Oregon Ducks New Look Offense Aug. 14 2024 at the Hatfield-Dowlin Complex in Eugene, Oregon; Oregon tight ends coach Drew Mehringer works with players during practice. Oregon dismissed Mehringer as offensive coordinator on Sunday. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Oregon has been able to move the ball this year but has struggled to put points on the scoreboard, evidenced by the 426 yards and 10 points on Saturday on the road at Illinois. Oregon has been able to move the ball this year but has struggled to put points on the scoreboard, evidenced by the 426 yards and 10 points on Saturday on the road at Illinois. In steps Johnson, who assumes primary play-calling duties for an offense that ranks tied for No. 93 in the nation for first down offense and No. 107 on third down (35.4 percent). For comparison, LSU leads the nation with 28 first downs per game to the Ducks’ 20.6. Johnson is tasked with revitalizing an offense that will be without star quarterback Dante Moore , who is not expected to return this season after a concussion forced him out of Oregon’s last three games, in which the Ducks scored a combined 42 points (14.0 per game) under backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Johnson, however, isn’t inheriting a shortage of talent. Leading Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart (352 yards, four touchdowns) is expected to return against the Wildcats. Wide receiver Dakorien Moore has stepped up with Stewart suspended, leading the Big Ten in receptions the last two weeks with 16 catches for 106 yards. Sept. 5, 2026; Eugene, Oregon; Oregon Ducks wide receiver Evan Stewart shakes off a Boise State Broncos' defender at Autzen Stadium. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Despite the rollercoaster month of October, Raiola has now thrown for 761 yards, six touchdowns and two interceptions, for a passing offense that ranks No. 25 in the FBS with 277.7 yards per game. Despite the rollercoaster month of October, Raiola has now thrown for 761 yards, six touchdowns and two interceptions, for a passing offense that ranks No. 25 in the FBS with 277.7 yards per game. Johnson’s true test might be getting Oregon’s ground attack going. The Ducks average 145.4 rushing yards per game (No. 90 in nation) and have yet to have a single-game 100-yard performance yet this season between running backs Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. The Ducks haven’t had a 100-yard effort since running back Noah Whittington rushed for 104 yards against USC during Week 12 of the 2025 season. Chip Kelly Returns to Autzen Oct 24, 2026; Evanston, Illinois, USA; Northwestern Wildcats tight end Alex Honig celebrates his touchdown reception against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at New Ryan Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Former Oregon coach Chip Kelly returns to Autzen Stadium, where he led the Ducks to a 46-7 record and four bowl appearances between 2009 and 2012. Former Oregon coach Chip Kelly returns to Autzen Stadium, where he led the Ducks to a 46-7 record and four bowl appearances between 2009 and 2012. The Northwestern offensive coordinator brings with him an offense that’s averaging 34.7 points and 435.6 total yards per game. The Wildcats generated much of the production out of the backfield, averaging 204.6 yards per game on the ground on 5.2 yards per carry. They go up against an Oregon defense allowing 127.9 rushing yards per game and 3.7 yards per attempt. The Ducks have been among the nation’s best at stopping opponents on third down (29.7 percent, No. 11 nationally), but face a Northwestern team that converts on 47.6 percent of its third down attempts. Lanning’s squad will be asked to slow down a Wildcats ground game that includes quarterback Aidan Chiles (nine rushing touchdowns) and running back Caleb Komolafe (551 yards, five touchdowns), one week after giving up 225 rushing yards to Illinois. Prediction and Betting Odds Oct 24, 2026; Champaign, Illinois, USA; Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola throws a pass against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Gies Memorial Stadium. That’s down from its opening valuation which saw Oregon favored by 7.5 points with an over/under of 50.5 points. The prediction: Kelly’s rushing attack eats up clock and yardage in the first half, but the Oregon defense doesn’t break. New offensive coordinator Jay Johnson opens up the Ducks’ playbook in the second half. Raiola, the running game and wide receiver Dakorien Moore put Oregon in a position to eke out a 24-21 win on a late field goal by placekicker Gage Hurych, who atones for the three missed kicks against Illinois. And the Ducks’ hopes of reaching the Big Ten championship stay mathematically alive for one more week. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions Before Oregon Ducks vs. Northwestern Wildcats
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions Before Oregon Ducks vs. Northwestern Wildcats Skip to main content SI.COM Transfer Portal FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2024 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM DUCKS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM DUCKS BB The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) will play host to No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten) on Saturday at Autzen Stadium in dire need of a win to keep their slim conference championship hopes alive. And do so against a familiar face when former Ducks coach (2009-2012) and current Wildcats offensive coordinator Chip Kelly returns to Eugene with a Wildcats team that arrives riding a four-game win streak and averaging 34.7 points per game. Oct 24, 2026; Champaign, Illinois, USA; Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola warms up before a game against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Gies Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Ron Johnson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oregon, conversely, has managed just 42 points (14.0 per game) in its last three contests. The scoring drought prompted coach Dan Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer with Jay Johnson now calling plays in an effort to breathe life into a stagnant Ducks offense. Oregon, conversely, has managed just 42 points (14.0 per game) in its last three contests. The scoring drought prompted coach Dan Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer with Jay Johnson now calling plays in an effort to breathe life into a stagnant Ducks offense. In a game featuring one of the Big Ten’s premier rushing quarterbacks versus a backfield looking to finally break out, it could very well be a special teams player that keeps Oregon’s fading hopes on life support. Running Back Dierre Hill Jr. Becomes First Duck to Top Century Mark Sept. 26, 2026; Los Angeles, California; Oregon Ducks running back Dierre Hill Jr. carries the ball against the USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Oregon has not had a 100-yard rusher since running back Noah Whittington gained 104 yards against USC during Week 12 of the 2025 season, a streak of 10 games. Oregon has not had a 100-yard rusher since running back Noah Whittington gained 104 yards against USC during Week 12 of the 2025 season, a streak of 10 games. Sophomore running backs Jordon Davison (88 carries, 436 yards, seven touchdowns) and Dierre Hill Jr. (79 carries, 397 yards, three touchdowns) have split carries this season. But neither has topped 100 yards in a game. Johnson’s new offense, however, arrives with new potential. Both Davison and Hill Jr. set season-bests in last week’s 21-10 loss to Illinois with 96 and 86 yards, respectively. Sep 26, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Oregon Ducks running back Dierre Hill Jr. reacts after rushing for a one-yard touchdown against the USC Trojans at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Hill Jr. presents an interesting option for Johnson out of the backfield, having caught 20 passes for 209 yards at 10.5 yards per catch. Hill Jr. presents an interesting option for Johnson out of the backfield, having caught 20 passes for 209 yards at 10.5 yards per catch. And now he’s knocking on the door to the 100-yard club. The closest he’s come to the century mark was the 94 yards he gained in just his third career game, against Northwestern in Week 3 of the 2025 season. A consistent run game has been lacking for Lanning’s squad this season, But the Northwestern defense can be vulnerable against the run where the Wildcats allow 152.7 yards on the ground per contest, ranking them No. 88 nationally. Prediction: Hill Jr.’s first-career 100-yard performance takes pressure off struggling quarterback Dylan Raiola. Quarterback Aidan Chiles’ Rushing Touchdown Streak Ends Oct 10, 2026; Evanston, Illinois, USA; Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles looks to pass against the Ball State Cardinals at New Ryan Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles has scored a rushing touchdown in all seven games this season for nine total to lead the team. The next closest teammate is running back Caleb Komolafe with five rushing scores. Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles has scored a rushing touchdown in all seven games this season for nine total to lead the team. The next closest teammate is running back Caleb Komolafe with five rushing scores. The streak ties him for the longest by a Wildcat since running back Noah Herron scored a rushing touchdown in seven-consecutive games in 2004. Oregon’s defense has allowed opponents to score on 19 of their 23 red zone possessions this season, but only four of them have come via rushing touchdowns. The Ducks are giving up an average of 127.9 rushing yards per game, but surrendered 225 against the Fighting Illini, including a 75-yard touchdown run, the sixth rushing score on the year allowed by Oregon. Prediction: Three of the four rushing touchdowns allowed in the red zone this year have come from quarterbacks Anthony Colandrea of Nebraska, Jayden Maiava of USC and Drew Mestemaker of Oklahoma State. That trend comes to a halt on Saturday as Chiles puts up yards, but fails to reach the end zone. Punter Bailey Ettridge Becomes Difference Maker Oct. 10, 2026; Eugene, Oregon; Oregon punter Bailey Ettridge punts the ball away versus the UCLA Bruins at Autzen Stadium. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect While the battle on the ground ensues, the deciding factor could come via the air. Specifically, on special teams, where Oregon punter Bailey Ettridge enters Saturday among the nation’s elite. While the battle on the ground ensues, the deciding factor could come via the air. Specifically, on special teams, where Oregon punter Bailey Ettridge enters Saturday among the nation’s elite. The sophomore has boomed 29 kicks for 1,353 yards at an average of 46.7 yards per punt, good for No. 8 in the country. All told, the Ducks rank No. 1 in the FBS in punt return defense, having held opponents to -6 return yards (-1.0 yards per kick) all year. Northwestern has struggled mightily on punt returns, averaging just 6.5 yards per return, placing them at No. 101 nationally. The Wildcats have a mere 39 punt-return yards all season with 26 of them coming on one return by wide receiver Drew Wagner against Penn State. Sep 26, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Oregon Ducks placekicker Gage Hurych celebrates with punter Bailey Ettridge after kicking a 19-yard field goal against the USC Trojans at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Fun fact: Ettridge himself has 26 career rushing yards on two carries. Prediction: The Australian native placed three punts inside the Illinois 20-yard line, giving him 11 for the season, along with seven kicks of 50-plus yards and only one touchback. He adds three more punts within the Northwestern 20 yard line on Saturday in Autzen, flipping the field in favor of Oregon and pinning Chiles and the Wildcats deep. picks.blurb: Oregon Gets Strong Prediction Before Northwestern Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Oregon Gets Strong Prediction Before Northwestern Showdown (Ron Johnson-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:09 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The 2026 season hasn't gone to plan for the Oregon Ducks , with the team underperforming compared to where it was expected to be. Oregon entered the year with high expectations to go after a title, but the team has faltered this season . The Ducks will be coming into this current week with a record of 4-3, with the team coming off a tough loss to Illinois. This week, the Ducks will be hosting the No. 20-ranked Northwestern Wildcats, offering this group a chance to grab a big win. Northwestern has been a major surprise this season, with the team going 6-1 to open the year. Oregon will be starting quarterback Dylan Raiola in the game, with starter Dante Moore now out for the remainder of the season. Raiola has seen his moments of success with the Ducks this year, but overall, he has struggled to play up to par. But the Ducks are going to need him to show up against Northwestern for this team to have a chance. Oregon can at least salvage the season a little but if they can pull out a victory at home this weekend. Heading into the game, college football analyst David Kenyon of Bleacher Report put out predictions for the matchups this week. Among these, Kenyon predicted that the Ducks will come away with a slim victory over Northwestern by a score of 21-19. Based on how the Ducks have played over the last few weeks, this seems to be an accurate prediction. Oregon has struggled to find its footing recently, but this is still a good team, especially ay home, where it's tough for opposing teams to play. With Raiola starting, the Ducks coaching staff is going to have to figure out a way to get him into better spots. Raiola has thrown for 761 yards with six touchdowns and two interceptions this season. Oregon fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following the loss to Illinois, and this could help the team be more explosive. Head coach Dan Lanning understood that some type of move needed to be made, and Mehringer ended up being the odd man out here. The Ducks will have to put points on the board to keep up with the explosive Northwestern offense. Quarterback Aidan Chiles has been great for the Wildcards this season, and he could cause real problems for Oregon in this game if the defense isn't careful. Kickoff between the Ducks and Wildcats is scheduled for 12:30 p.m. PT/3:30 p.m. ET from Autzen Stadium.

(Photo by Zoe Davis/Getty Images) | Getty Images Inside NU Archives · SB Nation Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:40 PM UTC · 10 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Northwestern has played itself into College Football Playoff contention. The 'Cats sit as the No. 20-ranked team in the nation, with six wins over South Dakota State, Colorado, Penn State, Michigan State, Ball State and Rutgers, and a narrow 29-23 loss on the road to the now No. 4-ranked Indiana Hoosiers. Thus far this season, they've passed the eye test, wowing pundits around the country with creative offensive formations and a turnover happy defense, but they are in need of quality wins over top-notch opponents. Over the next four weeks, NU will get three chances to secure resumé-changing victories, with matchups booked against Oregon, Iowa, Ohio State and Minnesota. The first of which, against Dan Lanning's Ducks, will take place on Saturday. Here's the INU staff's predictions for the 'Cats' road test against the 4-3 Oregon Ducks: Charlie Jacobs (27-16 Northwestern ) This Northwestern team has a different vibe to it. Although the Wildcats' last road trip was too close for comfort, Oregon has been struggling a lot lately and offers the perfect opportunity for Northwestern to pick up the win. Whether it's Brock Thomas or Dylan Raiola at quarterback, I'm not sure the Ducks can keep up with the Wildcats' offense, which will likely score enough no matter what. Plus, Chip Kelly back calling plays in Autzen… there's very few storylines better than that this week. Oregon, while a very talented roster, hasn't been able to put it all together. Even with a new offensive coordinator this week (or lack thereof), Oregon's offense has to prove it can compete for it to be threatening, even if the weapons are healthy. I'm taking the 'Cats. Jackson Pick (24-13 Northwestern ) Northwestern enters the meat of its schedule on a four-game winning streak, and at face value it's hard not to favor the 'Cats here. Aidan Chiles collected five total touchdowns against Rutgers on Saturday, with Caleb Komolafe adding one of his own to go with his 150 rushing yards on the day. Oregon, one of the preseason national championship favorites, has lost two of its last three, including a 21-10 shocker at Illinois that knocked it out of College Football Playoff contention. One reason for the Ducks' slide is obvious: their quarterback and potential No. 1-overall pick Dante Moore suffered a head injury against USC, and neither Dylan Raiola nor Brock Thomas have been able to sufficiently replace his production — Oregon has gone from 304 passing yards per game to just 205 since Moore's injury. On Saturday, Moore's continued absence will once again stifle an Oregon offense whose rushing attack hasn't produced enough to supplement its weakened passing game. While its defense has been stout enough, Northwestern will travel to Eugene with the strongest offense the Ducks have faced since their Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State. This game – if the Wildcats can win it – will begin to put the CFP in their sights. Autzen Stadium is a raucous environment to travel to for a NU team that's struggled on the road, and this is easily their biggest test since traveling to face Indiana. Unlike with the Hoosiers, though, the 'Cats don't need to execute at 100% to take this one. On another big day for the Wildcats' defense, Chiles will do just enough to escape Autzen with a season-defining victory. Donovan West (21-17 Oregon ) Five punts, three missed field goals and a fumble. That's how eight of Oregon's drives ended against Illinois last week. It was a masterclass in miscues from head coach Dan Lanning and the Ducks in a disappointing result that marked a season that has spun out of control. Despite a roster made up mostly of four- and five-star recruits, Oregon is 4-3 and has proven that raw talent doesn't automatically make a good football team. Northwestern, however, has proven the opposite. The 'Cats are an injury-ridden team of misfits that has united around a common goal and beaten the breaks off of three power conference teams. The only problem for NU is that its dominance has made the games boring to watch and has led to the Wildcat Wall leaving early.​ Yet, with the two programs on opposite trajectories, Oregon will still walk onto its home field on Saturday as favorites. The sports books trust the Ducks' depth and talent, and so do I. Their victories over USC and Nebraska, two wins more impressive than anything Northwestern has done, show that Oregon can still be a good football team. The Ducks will trot into Autzen Stadium knowing they need to win for any chance at making the playoff and grind their way to victory with a dominant performance in the trenches. As it did against Indiana, Northwestern will struggle to run the ball against Oregon, and Aidan Chiles won't be able to get it done through the air. The 'Cats' dreamy season will take a reality check, and expectations will be reevaluated. Zac Penson (24-17 Oregon ) I want to be wrong. The biggest hump I struggle to get over is that Oregon still has a stellar defense. Despite losing Dante Moore for the year, their experience and poise on defense is something they have continued to show over the past few weeks, allowing only 17 points to UCLA and just 14 points to Nebraska. Northwestern has also seemed to struggle on the road this season, falling to Indiana and squeaking out a win over Michigan State. And this stadium will be louder. Coming in at No. 20 on the AP Poll against an unranked Oregon team, the Wildcats have something to prove. Oregon lost to Illinois last week, so they clearly aren't invincible, but that was in Champaign. Autzen Stadium is a whole different animal. Despite losing to Illinois, Oregon is indeed favored. I would love to see the Cardiac 'Cats pull off the upset on this one, but I believe the pressure of the moment is only mounting for the Wildcats as the days drag on and they board their flight to Eugene. I believe Northwestern won't go down without a fight, though, and I expect this one to be a fun battle to the end. Whitley Williams (24-21 Northwestern ) Blurb: Strike while the opponent is weak. Northwestern is seeking its fifth consecutive win against the Oregon Ducks. Once considered a College Football Playoff contender, Oregon has endured a series of unexpected setbacks. The Ducks fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following their loss to Illinois. Once known for their explosive offense and "Pac-12 After Dark" spectacles, the Ducks are now a team searching for their identity. In many ways, the roles have reversed. Northwestern boasts a creative, explosive offense that keeps opposing defenses guessing. Offensive coordinator Chip Kelly will need to lean on that trickery against an elite Oregon defense that allows just 3.65 yards per carry and 197.6 passing yards a game. Assistant quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson will call the plays for Oregon on Saturday. With Dante Moore out for the season, Oregon will start Dylan Raiola at quarterback. Against Illinois, Raiola completed 66% of his passes for 246 yards but couldn't finish the job. The Wildcats will have to lock down deep-threat wide receiver Dakorien Moore. Aidan Chiles has played extremely tough on the road in hostile environments, and this test in Eugene will certainly show what the Wildcats are truly made of. Kussh Mital (21-10 Northwestern ) I don't see why this game should be any different than Oregon's previous matchup against Illinois. I believe this so much that I am predicting that same score in the Wildcats favor. Oregon's defense is great, don't get me wrong, but they just gave up over 200 rushing yards to Illinois, and Northwestern has a flat out better rushing attack. Moreover, Northwestern can air the ball out much more efficiently, something the Ducks have not had to deal with in a couple weeks. Aidan Chiles is the best quarterback Oregon has faced since Jayden Maiava, who threw for over 300 yards and two touchdown passes against it. Chiles probably won't do that, but he will certainly do some damage. However, the main issue for this Oregon squad is the quarterback position. When you can't trust your quarterback to run the offense effectively, it's hard to expect to win the game. Even with the return of some of the receivers for Oregon, Dylan Raiola is not going to get the job done against Northwestern. With the Wildcats somehow entering the game as underdogs, I expect them to wear that title with honor and make Oregon fans extra fearful on Halloween. Drew Christmann (23-16 Northwestern ) Since Dante Moore went down with a scary and controversial injury against USC, Oregon has a simple problem: they can't score. Since that Week 4 matchup in LA, the Ducks have scored no more than 17 points a game, down from 47.5 in prior games, including an 84-0 shutout against Portland. Now, after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following a loss to Illinois last week, in which the Ducks scored just 10 points, it's unclear what Oregon's offense will look like going forward, with Dan Lanning confirming he doesn't expect Moore to return for the rest of the season. Northwestern is the opposite. After years of a less-than-optimal offense, the Wildcats have been one of the conference's best, especially on the ground, where they average 204.6 yards per game. Aidan Chiles has been no slouch in the air, too, throwing for 1,617 yards with a 71.3% completion rate and just one interception. That, along with Chip Kelly's return to Autzen, makes for a scary matchup for Oregon. The ideal situation for the 'Cats' is a quick start, as it did against Rutgers last week, when they scored on the first three possessions of the game. But Northwestern has shown they know how to play from behind in hostile environments, like in Bloomington, where they scored 16 points in the final quarter to push defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the brink and at Michigan State in East Lansing, where Chiles drove 64 yards against his former school to win on a game-winning kick. The Wildcats have shown they can win both ways, and against an Oregon team whose season is spiraling, I see Northwestern moving to 7-1 on Halloween. Adam Sutro (27-24 Northwestern ) I have low confidence in Northwestern's defense entering this football game. A poor Rutgers offense killed the 'Cats on the ground last week, exposing a run defense issue that has been a problem all year for Northwestern. Fortunately for the 'Cats, Oregon has operated more through the air than on the ground for most of the season… though I think with all the talent the Ducks have on their offensive line, they will figure out how to expose the 'Cats' run defense and move the ball. Ducks Wire staff predicts Oregon Ducks vs. Northwestern Wildcats
picks.blurb: That seems like a long time ago, doesn't it? Less than a week later, we are sitting with the Ducks at 4-3, having just fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following another loss, and quarterback Dante Moore announcing that his 2026 season is over after the concussion he suffered earlier this year against USC. Now, with a laundry list of questions to answer, the Ducks go forward into a brutal home matchup against the No. 20 Northwestern Wildcats , hoping that they can somehow manage to get back to their winning ways. To preview the game, we go through our weekly roundtable with the writers from Ducks Wire to offer our opinions and predictions for what's to come. Here is our roundtable conversation. Question: Well, it's certainly been an eventful week in Eugene. Let's start with the biggest news: Dante Moore is not expected to play again this season. With the Ducks sitting at 4-3 and their playoff hopes essentially gone, what are your expectations for the rest of the season? What would a successful finish look like? Zachary Neel: At this point, a successful season is going 7-5 on the year and making it to a semi-respectable bowl game when all is said and done, and that's incredibly sad to say, considering where this season started. Just about everything has gone wrong for Oregon thus far, and I truly do see a reality where they struggle to even become bowl-eligible. But I think the culture wins out, and Dan Lanning can rally this team over the final five weeks. Bjorn Bergstrom: The culture that we’ve come to know in recent seasons is of a team that stays together and fights, no matter the circumstances. That hasn’t been the case in 2026, but if they can reclaim that fight and grittiness, then I think that should be considered a success. The way things are going, it’s hard to stamp “success” on a certain win total. It’s more about the process and the eye test, rather than the end result. Logan Brown: It’s hard to find any success in this season at this point. I guess if Oregon beats Washington, that’s probably the least you could ask for? I would say an 8-4 finish would mean the Ducks played well in November and finished strong, but that probably means losses to Northwestern and Ohio State. It’s probably going to get worse before it gets any better. Drew Mehringer Question: Dan Lanning made one of the biggest decisions of his coaching career on Sunday, firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer after Oregon's loss to Illinois. Do you agree with the decision, and how much of the blame for Oregon's offensive struggles falls on Mehringer compared to the players and other coaches? Zachary Neel: I think a change needed to be made, but I also don't think this change is going to lead to a switch being flipped for the Oregon offense. The problems go much deeper than just the play calling, in my opinion, and I don't think we're going to all of a sudden see the Ducks putting up 27-31 points per game because Mehringer is no longer in the building. As the OC, he was rightfully the guy to fall on the sword, but more changes are needed this offseason. Bjorn Bergstrom: It's hard not to agree with the decision. Fans had been on him from the very beginning, it seemed, but I was finally on board after last week’s debacle. As far as the blame, there’s some that goes to the position coaches who didn’t have their guys ready to play individually, but the play calls were what stuck out to me in particular. It didn’t seem like Mehringer had the ability to scheme up easy looks for his quarterbacks and easy running holes for his backs. There was a clear lack of creativity. Just watch any other top-25 team in college football and you’ll see the difference in outside-of-the-box thinking schematically that Mehringer just couldn’t manage to implement. Logan Brown: Unfortunately, I do feel like it was the right move. There were so many times where it just seemed like the offense was lacking situational awareness because of the play call. I lost count of the amount of times the Ducks ran a third down play, from any distance, where receivers were all running routes short of the sticks. There were zero aggressive calls, and more aiming and carefully crafting open receivers to the point where if the defense had an answer, there was no counter. I do think Oregon’s lack of offensive line and quarterback development has played a significant role in the offense’s struggles, but Mehringer was a clear issue that the Ducks could do something about midseason. New Play-Caller Question: Jay Johnson is taking over play-calling duties for the Ducks, and he'll have quite the challenge trying to turn this offense around. What's the biggest change you hope to see from Oregon's offense under Johnson? And realistically, how much improvement can we expect in just one week? Zachary Neel: Asking Johnson to come in and completely change this offense is unfair and unrealistic. I think at the best, you can hope that Oregon's offensive scheme looks more simplified, leaning more heavily on running between the tackles, finding a rhythm, and getting the ball past the sticks on down-and-distance situations. But as far as an entirely new scheme that looks different from what we've seen over the past seven weeks, I'm not expecting that. Bjorn Bergstrom: The biggest thing I’ll be wanting to see is more creativity in the passing game as far as Dylan Raiola’s platform, whether it be rolling him out, sprint-outs, or moving the pocket so it’s not a straight dropback. Moving the quarterback in the backfield makes it so much more difficult for a defense to pinpoint where he’ll be on a given play, opening up the run game at the same time as they’ll be just a step slower. Also, no more Wildcat. Yuck. Logan Brown: Take some chances! Oregon has nothing to lose at this point. The Ducks have Ferraris all over the offense, but most throws are horizontal or short of the sticks. Safeties play close to the line because the Ducks don’t trust their quarterback to air it out. At this point, the season is gone, so why not air it out? Why not run more counters and try to produce explosive plays on the ground? I don't think Johnson changes a ton in just one week, but I do think he could set the tone with a different plan on critical downs. Question: Northwestern comes to Eugene at 6-1, ranked No. 20 in the nation, with former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly running the offense. The Wildcats have been one of the biggest surprises in the Big Ten this season. What concerns you most about this matchup, and where do you think Northwestern has the biggest advantage over Oregon? Zachary Neel: Any time Oregon faces a true dual-threat quarterback who can beat you with his feet, Duck fans get worried. That has been the Achilles heel in Eugene for years, and Aidan Chiles is as good at that as anyone. With his ability both in the air and on the ground, plus Chip Kelly's offensive mind, I know that the Ducks' defense is going to have its hands full on Saturday. Bjorn Bergstrom: I think that Northwestern has a simple, yet very important advantage: they play sound, complementary football much, much better than the Ducks have this season. They’ve been a complete team, complimenting each other on offense, defense and special teams and picking up for the other when needed. That’s something Oregon hasn’t done this season, and I don’t expect them to on Saturday. Logan Brown: I’m so interested in this battle of the ground with Northwestern’s run game. They have a three-headed monster in the backfield, plus the mobility of quarterback Aidan Chiles. The Wildcats have run the ball so well this season, but it hasn’t always come easy on the road. Oregon has played the run better the past few weeks, but the Ducks couldn’t stop Illinois on the ground in the second half last week. If Northwestern runs the ball efficiently, they win with a huge advantage. If not, it can get interesting. Question: We've talked a lot about Oregon's offensive struggles, but the defense will have its hands full with Chip Kelly and a Northwestern offense that's been rolling this season. What's the biggest key for Oregon's defense to slow down the Wildcats and give the Ducks a chance to win? Zachary Neel: As I mentioned above, it's going to be all about slowing down the run for Northwestern. That means more than just Chiles, though. The Wildcats have a trio of very good running backs that can hurt you in different ways. If Northwestern is able to find success on the ground, it will open up the play-action passing game, where tight end Luke Dehnicke can be lethal. Bjorn Bergstrom: The biggest key is forcing Aidan Chiles to have an off day and revert back to his struggles from his first three seasons. During that time, Chiles was an erratic, turnover-prone passer lacking confidence. In 2026, he’s full of confidence and is an absolute baller, making plays that simply weren’t imaginable just 12 months ago. Getting in his face, making him feel pressure and not be able to get going with easy throws early is imperative for the Ducks. But with Kelly’s scheme, I lean towards Chiles being able to get going early. Logan Brown: I already talked about the run game, but the Ducks need to play disciplined against Chiles. The senior quarterback can burn them with RPO plays or just a regular read option. Northwestern utilizes the whole field with wide splits, so the pressure is on Oregon’s edge rushers more than ever to contain Chiles in the option and quick game and avoid getting caught too far up field. Gambling Corner Question: Gambling Corner: You get $100 to spread across the point spread (Oregon -3.5), and the Over/Under (47.5 points). How are you allocating your funds? Zachary Neel: Give me all $100 on Northwestern to cover. Vegas always knows something, but I don't know what in the world they've seen from the Ducks over the past month to consider them a 3.5-point favorite here. Bjorn Bergstrom: I think Northwestern will win, so I’m tempted to go there, but what in the world is pulling the over/under so high? Mehringer is gone but the bones of the offense are still here, along with a Ducks defense that has been dominant. I don’t see either team surpassing 24 points, so I’ll put all $100 on the under. Logan Brown: I’m putting $65 on Northwestern to cover the spread and the other $35 on the under. Northwestern’s offense is rolling right now, and Oregon’s is not, but I think both defenses could come to play on Saturday afternoon. Final Score Prediction Question: Who wins this game, and what is the final score? Zachary Neel: I've got Northwestern 27, Oregon 16. Bjorn Bergstrom: We’re about to see a Ducks team sitting at .500 as the calendar flips to November. Northwestern 20, Oregon 13. Logan Brown: Northwestern 24, Oregon 18. The Wildcats run the ball and grind the clock in the second half, and Oregon’s offense continues to struggle to find explosive plays. Oregon (4-3) sits in a familiar betting situation that sharps and the public have both aligned on over the past few years. Oregon is a -3.5 point favorite at home over #24 Northwestern (6-1), which certainly could be a head-scratcher to some. Oregon is coming off a 21-10 win over Illinois and struggled to get much of anything going after an opening drive touchdown. The Ducks went 4-of-15 on third downs, outgained the Illini 426-314 in total yards but had five punts, one fumble, and three missed field goals. The Ducks are out of the playoff race after the loss and are in a look-ahead spot to their bye week! The Ducks could use a break before going to Ohio State, then hosting Michigan for two of their final three games. Oregon could be in jeopardy of missing a bowl game if they lose here. Northwestern routed Rutgers 42-14 last weekend as Aidan Chiles threw for three touchdowns and ran for two more! It was a career day for Chiles as the Wildcats collected 502 yards of offense and posted an impressive 9-of-13 third-down mark. Rutgers averaged 3.7 yards per pass on 100 passing yards and were sacked four times. It was Northwestern’s most dominant performance defending the pass, but will it translate to the West Coast? Northwestern has had a trip out West all season, so it will be interesting to see if the time zone difference affects the Wildcats. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Oregon vs Northwestern Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Time: 3:30 PM Eastern Site: Autzen Stadium City: Eugene, OR TV/Streaming: NBC | Peacock Game Odds for Oregon vs Northwestern The latest odds as of Friday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Oregon Ducks (-175), Northwestern Wildcats (+145) Spread: Oregon -3.5 (-110) Total: 47.5 points Head Coach: Dan Lanning 2026 Record: 4-3 (2-2) Offensive Points Per Game: 33.1 (T-40th) Defensive Points Per Game: 20.7 (40th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 13th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 15th The Oregon Ducks Offense: Oregon had 112 more yards than Illinois last week, but couldn’t convert their drives into points as they either punted or missed a field goal in eight out of 12 drives. The Ducks are 8-of-42 on third downs during this three-game skid and has 10 turnovers. It’s no surprise they’ve fired their offensive coordinator after falling to 4-3 and scoring a season-low 10 points. Oregon Player to Watch on Offense: QB Dylan Raiola Dylan Raiola gets another start after going 27-of-41 for 246 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. Railoa took two sacks and fumbled twice, losing one, so it was far from a good start. The Ducks offense has spiraled in the wrong direction since Dante Moore ‘s injury. Railoa did lead a game-winning drive against his former Nebraska team and had an impressive second half in the win over USC, but the quarterback position has been a clear issue in why they’ve scored 42 total points in the last three games. The Oregon Ducks Defense: The Oregon defense has kept this team in games over the past three games. As the offense has averaged 14.0 points per game over the last three contests, the defense has given up 17.3 points per game and 20.7 points per game over the season. Oregon held Illinois to 89 passing yards and 4.7 yards per pass last week, but they did toss two touchdowns. The Ducks only had two sacks, but recorded five TFLs. The Ducks had a great start with four punts forced in the first five drives and a fumble on the other, but the defense unraveled in the second half. Illinois had 192 yards of offense, three punts, and two touchdowns on the final five drives. Oregon’s defense could limit Northwestern here, and honestly, that might be their only chance to win. Oregon Player to Watch on Defense: DL Matayo Uiagalelei Matayo Uiagalelei had his four-game sack streak snapped in the loss at Illinois. Uiagalelei leads Oregon with six sacks on the year and is sixth in tackles with 30. Northwestern runs a lot of misdirection and RPOs, so Uiagalelei will have plenty of sack and TFL opportunities. The rest of his season will be spent on raising his draft stock. Northwestern looks like a totally different offense with Chip Kelly, and he may put a little extra dip on his chip against his former team. Northwestern Player to Watch on Offense: QB Aidan Chiles Aidan Chiles is coming off a career-high five touchdowns versus Rutgers, three through the air and two on the ground. Chiles tossed 219 yards, his third straight over 200 yards and sixth out of seven games, plus a season-high 83 rushing yards and a long of 37 yards. Taking that momentum to the West Coast will be the challenge, but he should be up for it. Chiles had three touchdowns and an impressive second half at Indiana, plus 251 total yards and a win at Michigan State in Northwestern’s only road games. Chiles hasn’t thrown an interception on the road this season, but he has taken nine sacks. The Northwestern Wildcats Defense: Northwestern held Penn State (22) and Michigan State (89) below 100 rushing yards in conference play, but gave up over 200 yards to Indiana (201) and Rutgers (244). Which rush defense we see this weekend could dictate how much success Oregon has, especially since they have a new offensive coordinator taking over. The Wildcats held Rutgers to 100 total passing yards between two quarterbacks, forced three turnovers, and grabbed four sacks. It will be unclear what Oregon’s game plan is, but Northwestern is an opportunistic unit that can create pressure. I expect a lot of blitzes on Saturday. Northwestern Player to Watch on Defense: LB Brayden Brus Brayden Brus is coming off another stellar outing. Brus had 10 tackles and one sack against Rutgers. He has back-to-back games with double-digit tackles (15, 10), and in his two road games, Brus has 20 tackles and one sack. He leads the Cats with 62 tackles and four sacks after finishing third last year with 81 tackles and tied fourth with 2.5 sacks. Brus only had five tackles against Oregon last year, but I’d expect more than that this time around. away.headline: Iowa Football Injury Update: Hawkeyes Banged Up, Northwestern Face Huge Question Mark
away.blurb: Two of Iowa's starting defensive backs are nursing some sort of injury and are listed as questionable heading into this weekend's contest against Northwestern. Starting cornerback Jaylen Watson and the do-it-all safety Zach Lutmer are each trying to get ready to go on Saturday. Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles is questionable The most shocking name on the availability report is Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles. He is currently listed as questionable for the game this weekend, which completely changes the complexion of things if he isn't ready to go. He didn't exit Northwestern's last game against Oregon early with an injury, but he did go just 5-for-14 in the second half. Could that have been injury-related, or the Ducks' defense figuring out Northwestern a bit more as the game went on? My gut tells me Chiles is going this weekend, and in all honesty, is probably closer to 100% healthy than he is questionable for being able to play. One thing to watch, depending on what the injury is, could be his impact on the ground. You can tell that college football has hit the month of November. Not only are the temperatures about to begin dropping across Big Ten country, but the injury reports are starting to grow longer and longer each weekend for everyone in the conference. The Iowa Hawkeyes and Northwestern Wildcats have put together quite a lengthy availability report that features a total of 29 players listed on the report in some capacity heading into the weekend. Both teams see key players on the report, too, that raise some concerns. Iowa is thin on the offensive line After holding up for most of the year across the front, Iowa's offensive line is starting to see its depth go away in a hurry. Starting center Cael Winter is going to miss this game, along with key depth pieces Lucas Allgeyer, Trent Wilson, and Cannon Leonard. Iowa is paper-thin across the offensive line now. Fortunately, four of the five starters remain in the lineup, with Michael Myslinski slotting in at the starting center position in place of Cael Winter. Question marks in Iowa's secondary My intuition tells me Iowa is likely to have both of them, as neither seemed horribly banged up after the Wisconsin contest, but only time will tell, along with a pregame workout on the field, as to whether one or both of Watson and Lutmer are good to go. Kickoff is set for 4:15 p.m. ET on SEC Network. Oklahoma is favored by -5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -200. The total is set at 44.5 points. Here's my South Carolina vs. Oklahoma prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 31. South Carolina vs. Oklahoma Pick: South Carolina 1Q ML (+106) My Oklahoma vs. South Carolina best bet is on South Carolina to lead after the first quarter. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. South Carolina vs Oklahoma Odds, Point Spread, Betting Lines South Carolina vs Oklahoma point spread : Oklahoma -3.5, South Carolina +3.5 South Carolina vs Oklahoma over/under : 44.5 Total Points South Carolina vs Oklahoma moneyline : South Carolina ML +138, Oklahoma ML -165 South Carolina is the hotter of the two teams, and it got there by turning the offense over to LaNorris Sellers and the run game. The Gamecocks opened the season with a 57-0 rout of Kent State, then hit a rough stretch with losses to Mississippi State , Alabama, and Kentucky , with the Alabama game their only SEC loss by more than one score. Since then, they've won back-to-back games over ranked opponents. On Oct. 10, they rolled No. 16 Florida 38-19, with Sellers accounting for five touchdowns, four through the air and one on the ground, and last Saturday they beat No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 on a walk-off 48-yard field goal. Sellers had three touchdowns in that one, throwing for 210 yards and carrying 18 times for 96 yards, and the Gamecocks came out of the gate fast, going 75 yards in 10 plays on their opening drive and then scoring again on a 31-yard Sellers run to take a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. The strength of this team is its ground game, which leads the SEC at 218.3 yards a game. Sellers has 507 rushing yards at 6.0 a carry and Matt Fuller has 513 yards and five touchdowns, so defenses are forced to account for two backfield threats before Sellers throws a pass. The weak spots are in the trenches and on defense. The offensive line has allowed 15 sacks and is missing Josiah Thompson, Dayne Arnett and Seth Smith, receiver Jayden Sellers is also done for the season, and edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah is out. Defensive back Quay'sheed Scott and running back Jawarn Howell are doubtful. The defense ranks 119th in success rate , allows 222.7 passing yards a game, and has just four interceptions, which is why South Carolina's games tend to be decided by whether the offense keeps scoring. One key note: Shane Beamer, who was an assistant head coach for the offense at Oklahoma under Lincoln Riley, knows this program well. Oklahoma has been a defense-first team that is still looking for a consistent offense. The Sooners opened with a 51-0 win over UTEP , then lost to Michigan, beat New Mexico, and fell to Georgia before pulling off the season's biggest upset, a 27-24 win over then-No. 1 Texas on October 10 in the Red River Rivalry. They followed that with a 21-13 loss to No. 15 Kentucky at home, a game they led 13-7 into the fourth quarter before Mateer threw two interceptions, one returned for a touchdown, and last Saturday they beat Mississippi State 23-15 on the road. That win was their best offensive day of the season, 467 total yards, with John Mateer completing 22 of 29 passes for 283 yards and two touchdowns without a turnover and Isaiah Sategna catching eight passes for 164 yards, along with 184 rushing yards, well above their season average of 92.5. The identity is still their defense. Oklahoma ranks second in the SEC in total yards allowed and first in pass defense, with 22 sacks, and it ranks second in adjusted EPA per play and success rate. The offense is the problem. The Sooners rank last in the SEC in total offense, have the conference's worst run game and sit 121st in offensive success rate, and they've scored fewer than 30 points in six straight games, every SEC game this season included. Mateer has 1,591 passing yards, a 66.7% completion rate, 11 touchdowns and seven interceptions, and Sategna leads the receivers with 578 yards. Lastly, the injury list is long, with linebacker Taylor Heim, receiver Trell Harris, tight end Trynae Washington, cornerback Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Eddy Pierre-Louis and Ryan Fodje out; receiver Elijah Thomas doubtful; and Peyton and Eli Bowen and linemen Jake Maikkula and Fred Hinton questionable. The case for South Carolina in the first quarter starts with the price. At +106, the market is treating the first 15 minutes as close to a coin flip, while the full-game line has Oklahoma as a 4.5- to 5.5-point favorite and South Carolina's moneyline anywhere from about +150 to +175. That gap makes sense, because Oklahoma's advantages are the kind that build over four quarters: a defense that ranks near the top of the SEC and can grind an opponent down over four quarters. However, those advantages don't help much early in a game, and the early part of the game is exactly where South Carolina's offense has been at its best. The gap between the two offenses is the other piece. South Carolina has the SEC's top rushing attack, Oklahoma has the conference's worst run game and 121st-ranked success rate, and the Sooners have not been quick starters in their recent games. They trailed Kentucky 7-0 after the first quarter, and against Mississippi State their entire first-quarter output was a field goal. South Carolina, meanwhile, scored on both of its first two possessions against Tennessee and has a quarterback who can make a defense pay with one big play, as he did on the 31-yard run. Oklahoma's defense is excellent, but a Sellers-Fuller running game that forces it to defend the whole field is the kind of look that can produce a scripted score, and winning the quarter may only take one good drive. The weather may also tilt things toward the visitors. The forecast calls for rain on Saturday, most likely before kickoff, with a high near 65, and a damp field tends to favor the team that wants to run the ball. The Gamecocks also fell behind early in the Florida game before taking over, so a slow start is possible, but with a +106 price for what is likely a much closer first quarter than the full-game odds suggest, South Carolina is the better side. Pick: South Carolina 1Q ML (+106)

picks.headline: Staff Picks: Can Oklahoma Build on Last Week's Success Against South Carolina?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Can Oklahoma Build on Last Week's Success Against South Carolina? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer scans the defense before a snap against MSU. | Carson Field / Sooners On SI Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's going to be much harder to run the football this week against a stout South Carolina defense. If the Sooners can continue their upward trajectory against the Gamecocks, they'll have a chance. If not - if John Mateer has to lead the team in rushing attempts and the Sooners average less than 4 yards per carry, then desperation will set in, Mateer will be forced to make plays - then bad things will happen. But if OU can run the ball just a little, Mateer can relax and guys like Isaiah Sategna and Rocky Beers and Lloyd Avant can help out the defense by moving the chains, changing the scoreboard and winning a home game. Final: Oklahoma 21, South Carolina 13 John Mateer found a healthy headspace in Starkville, but Saturday will be the first real test to see if he can stick to the plan. South Carolina's defense is not impenetrable, but it's a much better group than Mississippi State's, with difference-makers who can wreck drives and put Mateer into tough situations. It's likely there will be a turnover, and the test will be if OU's quarterback can rebound after that. History says he'll have a tough time. Brent Venables' defense will get its third look at talented quarterback LaNorris Sellers, but if Oklahoma is unable to finish off drives, the Gamecocks have shown they can notch dramatic victories. Final: South Carolina 20, Oklahoma 13 Someone from the future could tell me a plethora of different outcomes from Saturday's game, and I'd believe them. Oklahoma's offense certainly made progress against Mississippi State, and it's possible that the Sooners build on those improvements at home against South Carolina. But it also wouldn't be shocking if OU's offense regressed into the turnover-prone unit that it was against Kentucky, Georgia, New Mexico and Michigan. South Carolina comes into Norman on a two-game winning streak after ranked victories over Florida (on the road) and Tennessee - the Gamecocks seem like they're due for a letdown. While South Carolina's defense is better than Mississippi State's was, there are plenty of areas for the Sooners to expose, assuming they can play a similarly clean game on Saturday. Oklahoma needs a win to stay above .500, and I expect the Sooners to earn a close victory over the Gamecocks. Final: Oklahoma 20, South Carolina 17 The Gamecocks are more dangerous than Mississippi State, on both sides of the ball. Last week was a small step forward for the Sooners' offense, nota giant leap. Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't completely fixed just because he had a solid game against the Bulldogs. But with Michael Fasusi back on the offensive line, the Sooners' offense adds layers. They don't have to have every element working in order to be successful. What they do need to do, though, is protect the football and keep up their strong defensive play. This game will be back and forth and figures to go down to the wire, but in the end, Oklahoma does just enough to start its first winning streak of the season. Brady Trantham The 2026 season is still up in the air. One thing it has told us is that basically no one has been able to handle a big emotional win and follow that up with another win a week later. South Carolina's win over Tennessee was very much an emotional win against a highly-ranked opponent - the Volunteers themselves had just beaten Alabama the week prior. OU has slowly built consistency on offense, just enough that paired with an elite defense, victories against flawed teams are realistic. The Sooners have proven to be great at corralling mobile quarterbacks and will showcase that again, while John Mateer will build off a great performance last week against a dangerous but very gettable defense. away.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners have had lengthy availability reports for much of the season, but the Wednesday night report ahead of their game against South Carolina is long. Fifteen players are listed on the initial injury update; eight players are already ruled out for Week 9. On offense, key players Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, he provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to its interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, though he could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had ups and downs for the Sooners the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert High School graduate hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and played fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. Defensively, the Oklahoma Sooners have big questions. Rotation linebacker Cole Sullivan was ruled out for this week. Safety Peyton Bowen and cornerback Eli Bowen are both questionable for Week 9. Both Bowens are key pieces to the Sooners' defense, and against a good South Carolina passing attack, Peyton Bowen's presence is critical. He's one of the best safeties in college football. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli Bowen is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. He's been solid since entering the starting lineup against the Texas Longhorns and would need to be at his best this week if called upon to start. Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. The other player to watch on the offensive line is center Jake Maikkula. Maikkula was injured in the win over Mississippi State and was replaced by Caleb Nitta. Nitta played well, and Oklahoma will need him again this week against the Gamecocks if Maikkula can't play. If Nitta gets the start, it would be the eighth straight game the Oklahoma Sooners have used a new starting offensive line combination. Also on offense, starting wide receiver Elijah Thomas will not be back this week after missing the Mississippi State game. That likely means another start for Manny Choice and perhaps Parker Livingstone when the Oklahoma Sooners are in three-wide receiver sets. home.headline: Oklahoma vs. South Carolina: Initial injury report for Week 9
home.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners have had lengthy availability reports for much of the season, but the Wednesday night report ahead of their game against South Carolina is long. Fifteen players are listed on the initial injury update; eight players are already ruled out for Week 9. On offense, key players Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, he provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to its interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, though he could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had ups and downs for the Sooners the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert High School graduate hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and played fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. Defensively, the Oklahoma Sooners have big questions. Rotation linebacker Cole Sullivan was ruled out for this week. Safety Peyton Bowen and cornerback Eli Bowen are both questionable for Week 9. Both Bowens are key pieces to the Sooners' defense, and against a good South Carolina passing attack, Peyton Bowen's presence is critical. He's one of the best safeties in college football. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli Bowen is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. He's been solid since entering the starting lineup against the Texas Longhorns and would need to be at his best this week if called upon to start. Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. The other player to watch on the offensive line is center Jake Maikkula. Maikkula was injured in the win over Mississippi State and was replaced by Caleb Nitta. Nitta played well, and Oklahoma will need him again this week against the Gamecocks if Maikkula can't play. If Nitta gets the start, it would be the eighth straight game the Oklahoma Sooners have used a new starting offensive line combination. Also on offense, starting wide receiver Elijah Thomas will not be back this week after missing the Mississippi State game. That likely means another start for Manny Choice and perhaps Parker Livingstone when the Oklahoma Sooners are in three-wide receiver sets. home.headline: How Oklahoma State Could Deal with Tate Romney, Jaleel Johnson Injuries
home.blurb: The veterans came out of Saturday’s game with Iowa State dealing with injuries. Head coach Eric Morris told reporters on Tuesday that Oklahoma State was hopeful that both could play this week. Johnson is in his fifth season with the Cowboys and has 16 tackles and two sacks. He missed several games last year with an injury and was named a starter coming out of fall camp. He had his arm in a sling late in the game at Iowa State. Morris essentially ruled out tight end Carson Kolb on Tuesday. The redshirt sophomore, who suffered an injury to his left foot against Colorado, did not play against Iowa State. Morris said it “wouldn’t be this weekend” for Kolb’s return and that he would probably need a week or two more. Oklahoma State Designates Carson Kolb as Out for Iowa State Game The Oklahoma State Cowboys will be tracking the statuses of both linebacker Tate Romney and defensive end Jaleel Johnson this week. That means it’s likely that the pair will be on the Cowboys ’ player availability report all week – and that they’ll need to make sure they have a backup plan in case one or both are unable to play against the Kansas State Wildcats on Saturday. Replacing Tate Romney and Jaleel Johnson Romney has been Oklahoma State’s starter at MIKE linebacker all season and has already tallied a career-best 61 tackles with 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble. He previously had 52 tackles in 2023 with Arizona State. He finished the Iowa State game with nine tackles. OSU could go a couple of different directions if he cannot play. His direct backup on the depth chart is Taurean Davis, who has not started a game this year and had only one tackle this season. The Cowboys would more likely turn to Isaiah Chisom, who is listed as the starter at will linebacker but doesn’t start due to OSU’s 4-2-5 alignment. But he has 42 tackles alongside Romney and SAM linebacker Ethan Wesloski. Safety Quinton Hammonds had his arm in a sling in the later stages of the Colorado game but played against Iowa State. It’s not clear how serious Johnson’s injury is or if it’s similar. Malik Charles could start if Johnson cannot go. He has seen significant playing time as a backup and has 15 tackles and 3.5 sacks, along with an interception. Keviyan Huddleston started the only game that Johnson did not and is similar in body type. He could draw his second start of the year, based on the matchup. Huddleston has 17 tackles and a sack. Without him, Oscar Hammond received most of the snaps at tight end against Cyclones as he caught one pass. Hammond was at North Texas last year but didn’t play due to an injury. Morris did call Hammond the team’s best downfield threat at tight end going into that game. home.blurb: The status of McCloud, who is listed as out on the SEC's intitial availability report, will be re-evaluated after Saturday night's contest. A 6-foot-3, 294-pound sophomore from Georgia, McCloud has started five of eight games for the No. 24 Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) and has 22 tackles, second to senior Brendan Bett's 23, a team-high six quarterback hurries and three pass break-ups, tied for the team lead. Meanwhile, sophomore receiver Vernell Brown III is on track to miss his fifth straight game with a right knee injury after he was listed as doubtful. After Brown aggravated the injury during practice last Wednesday, his knee was drained Thursday. On Monday, medical staff performed a platelet-rich plasma procedure to try to accelerate healing. Receiver Bailey Stockton has filled the void , but he's listed as questionable after he led the Gators with eight receptions for 76 yards, including 41 after catch, and had 31 yards on two punt returns during last weekend's loss to Georgia. Also questionable is defensive end Emmanuel Oyebadejo, who has started four of the past five games and whose 4.5 sacks are tied for the team lead with Jayden Woods. The 6-foot-6, 303-pound Jacksonville State transfer also has five QB hurries and three pass break-ups. Three Gators other than McCloud are listed as out against Oklahoma, including starting right tackle Emekga Ugori. Senior Caden Jones, who started 10 games in 2025, will replace him. Tight end Evan Chieca also will not play against the Sooners. picks.headline: Advanced Analytics Predict Clemson vs. Florida State
picks.blurb: Advanced Analytics Predict Clemson vs. Florida State Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET BASKETBALL NEWS Every year, the Clemson Tigers meet the Florida State Seminoles in ACC play in what is an annual rivalry in the conference. In 2026, it happens to fall on Halloween. The Tigers are looking to bounce back from a loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies last weekend, falling to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. Now, head coach Dabo Swinney enters a hostile environment at Doak Campbell Stadium, looking to turn it around. However, the advanced analytics say otherwise. Versus Sports Simulator predicts the Tigers will lose by double digits, which would be the third time this season that they do so if the score is replicated. The model has Florida State winning by a score of 30-20, giving the Seminoles a 71% chance to win on Saturday. Since Clemson has begun to slip in games, the Tigers’ chance to win this game has dropped. Going into the season, Swinney’s group had a 45% chance to win at Tallahassee, but the offensive struggles throughout the season have seen those odds plummet. The lowest it got for the Tigers was after the loss to Miami, only holding a 22% chance. While Versus grades Clemson’s defense at a B grade, the Tigers’ C+ offense is what sets them back in this game. Meanwhile, Florida State’s offense is graded at a B+, led by dual-threat quarterback Ashton Daniels, and the plethora of weapons around him on the Seminole offense. It’s also important to note that this game has only been picked wrong once by the model, which was last year in Clemson’s home win. Otherwise, the advanced analytics typically follow how the game goes in terms of picking a winner. The game script is simple for Swinney: his offense has to play better, especially through the air. The glaring issue is that Clemson has only two passing touchdowns on the year, which is the fewest in the FBS in its seven games played this season. If the Tigers can get a score through the air, or even pick up first downs from throwing the football, they will have a shot at taking down the Seminoles in their own building yet again. However, we have yet to see that often thus far. Especially in an away environment, Clemson will have to be sound on both sides of the football, maybe even winning the turnover margin, to win as an underdog on Saturday night. If not, it could end up being a trick instead of a treat on the gridiron. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m., and the game will be broadcast on the ACC Network.
