picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Clemson Tigers | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation November 5, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football FSU looks to get to .500 and avoid 3rd straight loss as home favorites The Florida State Seminoles will host the Clemson Tigers this Saturday for a Halloween evening rivalry game at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee. The kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m., and the game will be televised by the ACCN. This will be the 39th meeting between the teams, with Florida State (3-4, 1-3 ACC) leading the all-time series 21-17, including a 12-7 record at Doak and an 18-15 record as ACC members. However, Clemson has won the last two meetings and holds a 15-7 advantage over the last 22 games, including wins in nine of the last 10 meetings. Clemson will be attempting to win a fifth consecutive game at Doak, becoming only the third program ever to win five consecutive road games against FSU in Tallahassee, joining Florida (six straight from 1966-76) and Miami (Fla.) (five from 1957-77). Despite Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State combining for 13 of the last 15 ACC championships, both teams are struggling this year. Clemson’s losses have come against #15 LSU, #1 Miami, and a 6-2 Virginia Tech team that scored the winning touchdown with 1:44 left on the clock. FSU’s four losses were in double overtime at #1 Miami, at #10 Alabama, at home against #19 SMU, and at Louisville when the defense totally collapsed. Clemson’s defense is the strength of their team. The Tigers rank 32nd in total defense (317), 36th in passing (186), T-53rd in rushing defense (131), T-30th in third-down defense (holding opponents to a 33.3-percent conversion rate), have allowed only four passing touchdowns, and have recorded 20 sacks through seven games. The Tigers’ passing offense, behind true freshman QB Tait Reynolds, who was named starter following an injury to Christopher Vizzina in their 2nd game, has only thrown one touchdown, and the 2 QBs combined have only thrown 2 TDs all season. Reynolds has been sacked 20 times this season and has thrown 3 interceptions while averaging just 6.1 yards per completion. Overall, Clemson has allowed 21 sacks, rank 115th in total offense (333). 112th in scoring offense, 115th in passing offense, 126th in 3rd-down conversion (31.7%), and 93rd in red zone offense. Florida State looks to avoid its 3rd straight loss after a heartbreaking double-overtime loss to Miami. The Noles were able to rush for 138 yards against the nation’s #1-ranked rushing defense; however, leading rusher Ousmane Kromah sustained a lower-leg injury and will miss the rest of the 2026 season. FSU loses double-overtime heartbreaker to Miami Social media reactions to the end of FSU vs. Miami Column: ACC replay review never entertained another outcome on FSU’s final play FSU running back Ousmane Kromah carted off near the end of first half against Miami Despite having a losing season record, FSU’s offense is ranked T-49th in the nation in total offense, 50th in scoring, 46th in rushing, 63rd in passing, and 34th in red-zone offense. FSU individual leaders After allowing Miami to rack up 583 total yards on 78 plays for a 7.5 yard average/play, FSU’s defense now ranks 130th in the nation, giving up 435 yards/game, 124th in passing defense (256 yards/game), T-112th in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert nearly 43% of the time on third-down attempts, and T-104th in first-down defense, allowing their opponents 155 first downs (22.1/game) in the 7 games played this season. Florida State is currently trending as a 5.5-point favorite with the over/under set at 49.5 points, according to FanDuel. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Clemson Tigers Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Jordan Silversmith (season record: 6-1) This game is a tricky one to call. I do not think Clemson is a good football team. However, they probably have the best unit on the field: their defense. Another issue for Florida State is that the Seminoles have historically struggled against the Tigers, with no home wins in the last decade. Even so, FSU should win on Saturday night. I imagine that, off a bye, head coach Mike Norvell will scheme up points on the opening drive, and Tony White’s defense should make forcing CU to throw the name of the game. This game will be close, as it often is with FSU, but Clemson isn’t good enough right now to win a rivalry game on the road. Seminole win, but no cover. FSU 27, Clemson 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 6-1) This could be a scary game, fitting for Halloween. With Kromah out, Clemson’s defense may keep FSU in check but the Tiger’s offense is dreadful. If Clemson somehow overwhelm’s Tony White’s defense, that relationship needs to end. I think FSU wins but it will be ugly. FSU 24, Clemson 17 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-2 ) Call me crazy, but this game is going to be completely unwatchable but FSU will emerge victorious. Firstly, it’s at Doak. On Halloween. Where else would you rather be? In all seriousness, Clemson’s offensive efficiency is dreadful. Like, REALLY dreadful. Per Game On Paper , Clemson’s EPA per pass is #136 out of #138 and their EPA per rush is #110. They are only 33.7% successful on third down, good for #128, and they are just bad at most things offense, mainly because their QB is a freshman. Their defense is good to great, though! #13 in EPA/Pass defense and just middle of the pack on rushing defense, #64 in the nation. Florida State meanwhile… their defense is trash. #127 on EPA per pass, #105 on EPA per rush, #120 on 3rd/4th down stops. The offense is good, though. #39 in EPA/Pass, #36 in EPA/Rush. If they can handle Clemson’s terrible offense and do good things on defense against a very not good Clemson offense, it might be a fun halloweekend in Tallahassee. Give me the Noles to pull off, not an upset per se, just a good, scrappy win. Florida State 14, Clemson 13 Curt Weiler (season record: 5-2, 2-5 ATS) Call me crazy for buying in again but I think I believe in this FSU team more than I do that Clemson team. The Tigers’ defense is pretty good. But the offense is very bad. Clemson is the only FBS team which has scored more points from its defense/special teams than its offense . To Tony White and his unit, I would say “If not now, when?” FSU 27, Clemson 20 NoleThruandThru (season record: 7-0) I’m taking a break from the Marshawn gag this week to honor my dad, who passed away two weeks ago. The world lost a wonderful FSU alum and fan, and I hope he enjoys this one from heaven. FSU 28, Clemson 24 Jon Marchant (season record: 6-1 ) Nobody knows what kind of team FSU will be from week to week. No result is off the table and there’s no score that would surprise anyone. So I’m picking FSU this week. Just cause. Also, it’s funny when Dabo loses. Clemson 23, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 5-1) I’m picking FSU but I don’t feel great about the prediction. I’m really worried about what FSU’s offense will look like without Kromah vs. Clemson’s defense. That being said I have not seen enough from Clemson’s offense to stay off the field and if you give FSU’s skill group enough shots they’re going to get points. Noles win. FSU 24 Clemson 17 Matt Minnick (Season record: 5-2; ATS: 4-3) As others have said, Clemson’s offense is putrid. Two passing touchdowns all season long is nearly unfathomable. But is Tony White’s defense just what the doctor ordered? It’s the moveable object vs the stoppable force. I’ve said all year that despite all the suckage over the last three seasons, FSU has honestly been pretty decent at home. However, Norvell’s teams also have a penchant for finding ways to lose very winnable games. If Kromah was healthy, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If Quindarious Jones was healthy I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If a random FCS DC who’s name was drawn out of a hat was FSU’s defensive coordinator, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. Clemson 30 , FSU 28 Frank DNole (season record: 3-4) FSU’s offense is better than Clemson’s defense. Clemson’s offense is about as good as FSU’s defense. Advantage Noles. This will be the game that turns the program around, and everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are 5.5-point favorites for a reason. Vegas knows something and the Seminoles know it too. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed against Virginia. The Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Clempsun opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, Orange Dabo’s 27 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 4-3, 3-4 ATS) For all its flaws over the last two seasons, FSU has taken care of business against the teams it should beat while in the confines of Doak. I have faith in FSU’s ability to get enough points against a stout Clemson defense and, as naive as it might be, take care of business against a dreadful Tigers offense. picks.blurb: Clemson Tigers final odds and prediction for Week 9 at Florida State Seminoles Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball and softball FanSided NCAA Sites Clemson has been left with no choice but to pick up the pieces after last week's soul-crushing loss to Virginia Tech. It may have only counted as one defeat on the ledger, but it really did feel like 2.5 losses mentally. For better or worse, the Tigers must turn the page and get ready for potentially a wild road game at the rival Florida State Seminoles. It will be during Halloween, nevertheless, so get ready for it. Clemson enters play at 4-3 on the season and 2-2 in the ACC. It has wins over Georgia Southern, North Carolina, Cal, and Charleston Southern, with losses to LSU, Miami, and Virginia Tech. While Florida State is only 3-4 on the season, Mike Norvell's Seminoles have a knack for scoring points and playing some fairly competitive football at home. Dabo Swinney cannot let his team overlook FSU. With that all in mind, here are the latest betting odds, how to watch this game, and a game prediction. Latest betting odds for Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles According to the FanDuel Sportsbook , Florida State will be laying 5.5 points to visiting Clemson. The associated moneylines for this game are Florida State -215 and Clemson +180. This means that it would take a $215 bet on Florida State to win $100, while wagering $100 on Clemson would pocket you $180. The projected point total for the game comes in at a combined 49.5 points, down from 51.5. Using all of that information above, a projected final score for this game would be something in the vicinity of Florida State 27.5, Clemson 22. While the odds for this game have fluctuated a bit , Florida State has been the favorite throughout for two reasons. It is a home game for the Seminoles, and the meager Tigers' offense has struggled to score points against Power Four competition all season long. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. How to watch Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles Here is what you need to know to be able to watch Clemson take on Florida State on Halloween night. Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 Time: 7:00 p.m. ET Location: Tallahassee, FL Venue: Doak Campbell Stadium TV Info: ACCN Streaming Info: fuboTV Radio: 105.5 FM (The Roar)/Clemson Athletic Network Kickoff from Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, FL, will be at 7:00 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. The ACC Network will carry the conference rivalry game. You can stream the game on fuboTV. You can listen to the game over the airwaves on 105.5 FM The Roar, or you can check out any other radio affiliates on the Clemson Athletic Network. You are not going to want to miss this rivalry game! Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles game prediction This high-stakes ACC rivalry game will come down to one of two things. From the Florida State perspective, it will be all about how disciplined the Seminoles' pass defense will be. This team can score points, but it does love to give them up in bunches. As for Clemson, the Tigers need to show on offense that they can put up 30 or so points if they need to get into some sort of a low-end shootout. Right now, it is so hard to fathom Clemson getting into the end zone at least three times on Saturday. The Tigers are going to need three touchdowns, and presumably 12 points from Nolan Hauser on special teams, to realistically have a chance at pulling off the upset. Gideon Davidson may get one on the ground, possibly two if he gets lucky. This will come down to whether Tait Reynolds can throw for one. Unfortunately, Clemson's offense is not built right now to score quickly and in bunches, so it will lose. Week 9 final score prediction: Florida State 30, Clemson 24. By Michael Schwartz in College Football Published: October 31, 2026 at 3:56 pm EDT Clemson visits Tallahassee for a Halloween night ACC showdown Red-zone finishing and run defense headline this Saturday night matchup Read below for my Clemson vs Florida State prediction and picks As the Clemson Tigers (4-3) hit the road to face the Florida State Seminoles (3-4), both teams find themselves desperate for a bounce-back victory. Florida State enters this ACC clash fresh off an Oct. 24 bye week following a hard-fought 43-35 defeat against Miami, while the Tigers recently stumbled in a tight 20-16 home loss to Virginia Tech. With both squads going 1-2 over their last three outings, finding a rhythm before November is paramount. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET this evening under the lights at Bobby Bowden Field at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Florida. The home squad will look to lean on its passing attack to defend its turf, while the visiting Tigers must rely on their stingy defense to grind out a road upset. In this preview, we break down both teams' recent form, highlight the key statistical mismatches and outline our Clemson vs Florida State picks for this Saturday night showdown, using the current college football odds as a starting point. Clemson vs Florida State Prediction Clemson vs Florida State prediction: Florida State covers at home in a game that clears 51.5 points. Florida State's offensive production dwarfs Clemson's sluggish attack. The Seminoles score touchdowns on 75% of their red-zone trips (21 of 28), while the Tigers sit at 39.1% (9 of 23). Clemson's defense is the best unit in this game, allowing just 21.3 points and 317.0 yards per game, but its offense has given it little support. Clemson vs Florida State Picks Clemson vs Florida State Pick #1: Florida State -6.5 Pick: Florida State -6.5 (50¢ on Polymarket) Florida State enters this matchup possessing a substantially more potent offense. The Seminoles are racking up 31.6 points and 414.3 total yards per game, easily outpacing Clemson's 21.4 points and 333.1 yards per contest. A critical differentiator in this game will be third-down efficiency; Florida State extends drives at a 41.8% clip, while the Tigers move the chains at just 31.7%. Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels is a true dual threat. He has amassed 1,618 passing yards and 12 passing touchdowns against eight interceptions, while adding 354 rushing yards and 11 scores on the ground. Contrast this with Clemson's Tait Reynolds, who has thrown for 1,096 yards with one touchdown against three interceptions this season. At 50¢, the spread is priced as a coin flip. Given their superior scoring ability and red-zone finishing, the Seminoles have the firepower to cover this number. Clemson vs Florida State Pick #2: Over 51.5 Pick: Over 51.5 (48¢ on Polymarket) Florida State's offense is high-scoring, but its defense is generous, surrendering 434.9 total yards and 27.9 points per game. Over their last three games, the Seminoles' run defense has regressed, allowing 230.3 rushing yards per contest. Clemson running back Gideon Davidson (492 rushing yards, five touchdowns) should find room to exploit that vulnerability. Combining the two teams' season scoring averages puts this game right around 53 total points, above the 51.5 line. Both teams also carry a -4 turnover margin, and short fields created by giveaways can lead to quick points. At 48¢, the Over implies a 48% chance of cashing. Florida State's scoring and its defensive problems make that the side I prefer. Clemson vs Florida State Saturday Night Odds Florida State +6.5 (52¢) -6.5 (50¢) Over 51.5 (48¢) Under 51.5 (54¢) Current Polymarket buy prices establish Florida State as a clear home favorite, with its moneyline at 68¢ against 34¢ for Clemson. The spread is close to a dead heat, with Florida State -6.5 at 50¢ and Clemson +6.5 at 52¢. On the total, the Under (54¢) is priced above the Over (48¢), so the market leans slightly toward a lower-scoring game. For Clemson, finishing drives is the biggest question mark: the Tigers reach the red-zone, but nine touchdowns on 23 trips caps their scoring ceiling. away.headline: Clemson’s Battered Offense Suffers Another Blow
away.blurb: Clemson’s battered offense absorbed another potential blow ahead of Saturday’s road test against Syracuse, as starting wide receiver Tyler Brown was listed as questionable on the initial Atlantic Coast Conference availability report . The Tigers are also uncertain about freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III, who is listed as questionable . Sellars missed the past two games with a concussion and suffered a setback in Monday’s practice. The perimeter uncertainty compounds significant absences already announced by head coach Dabo Swinney . Clemson will play without starting center Harris Sewell, who is sidelined for at least two weeks, while left guard Elyjah Thurmon was officially ruled out under concussion protocol after suffering a head injury against Florida State. In the backfield, starting running back Gideon Davidson is out with an ankle injury that Swinney tabbed as “day-to-day,” while reserve linebacker Kobe McCloud is also sidelined. The Orange face significant health questions of their own, headlined by starting quarterback Steve Angeli, who is listed as questionable . Angeli missed three games midseason for treatment on an Achilles injury originally sustained at Clemson to end his 2025 campaign . On the season, Angeli is averaging 237 passing yards with seven touchdowns against five interceptions. Syracuse's depth chart behind center could be stretched thin if Angeli cannot go, as backup quarterback Malachi Nelson is listed as doubtful . Elsewhere on the roster, starting defensive end Tunmise Adeleye and backup center Matthew Hawn are listed as questionable . On a more encouraging note for Syracuse, starting center Khalil Stewart and co-starting defensive lineman Dillan Fontus are both listed as probable . home.blurb: Clemson’s Elyjah Thurmon carted off field after suffering serious injury vs. Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Brad Taningco, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Sun, November 1, 2026 at 2:28 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Dabo Swinney and the Clemson Tigers are hoping to make up for their disappointing loss to Virginia Tech against Florida State. However, both teams took a moment to think about something other than the game after offensive lineman Elyjah Thurmon suffered a serious head-to-head collision. Clemson's entire team went onto the field in concern for their teammate, while Florida State players also took a knee as Thurmon was getting treatment. Thurmon was eventually carted off the field , and he was able to raise his right hand to give a thumbs up to the applauding crowd. The offensive lineman was trying to block during a running play early in the second quarter. But as several players converged onto the ball, he was hit in the head and was unable to get back up. Thurmon is in his third year at Clemson. After appearing in 11 games in his first two season, he has featured in seven of the team's first eight games. Despite the concern of seeing one of their teammates carted off with a serious injury, Clemson was able to rally and take a 23-10 lead into halftime. They scored 13 points in a row after Thurmon's injury thanks to two field goals and a Tait Reynolds touchdown pass to Olsen Patt-Henry. Like Florida State, Clemson is desperate to pick up the win amid a disappointing season thus far. Apart from a victory against North Carolina, they don't have any other quality wins to speak of. Nevertheless, Dabo Swinney will be looking to finish the season strong and hopefully get more recruiting wins in the process. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Miami looks to stay unbeaten against a sneaky-good North Carolina team on the road Getty Images Prior to last week, Miami had not held the No. 1 spot in the AP Top 25 poll since 2002, but so far the Hurricanes are looking every bit the part of the best team in the country. Not only have they raced out to a 7-0 start this year, but they've done so in a way that suggests a continuation of the success that led Miami all the way to the national championship game last season. With a 14-1 record in its last 15 games, Miami has been one of the best teams in the country since early November 2025, and now each week provides yet another opportunity for this year's team to validate that high poll ranking. This week, that means a trip to Chapel Hill to take on Bill Belichick and North Carolina in a game that offers Cristobal and Miami a chance to reverse a recent skid in the series. The Tar Heels have won their last five meetings in the series, including a 2-0 record against Cristobal with wins in 2022 and 2023. But those two Miami teams finished a combined 12-13 overall, while this year's group is clearly playing on a different level. For starters, those teams didn't have not just one but two Heisman Trophy contenders like Miami does this year with quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney . Those last teams that lost to North Carolina also didn't carry the nation's best scoring margin, as Miami does currently, beating opponents by 33.7 points per game. There's some history that favors UNC, sure, but Miami's strength will challenge the impact of the past. Miami vs. North Carolina: Need to know Tar Heels looking to bounce back from upset home loss: While Miami validated its position at No. 1 last week with a thorough thrashing of Pitt, North Carolina saw some of the hype for this matchup cooled by an upset loss at home to Syracuse . The Tar Heels led by 10 points in the fourth quarter but let Steve Angeli and the Orange offense back into the game with a couple late scores before eventually falling in overtime. That's brought even more urgency to Bill Belichick's crew to have their game locked in for Saturday night, because the kind of failure at the margins that led to the fourth-quarter collapse will only be exposed more dramatically against a team of Miami's caliber. The Tar Heels have shown in wins over TCU , Pitt and Duke that they can play a tight game and come out on the right side of close margins, but those victories (and certainly any upset effort against Miami) require a cleaner effort than North Carolina showed against Syracuse last week. A Saturday showcase spot for Miami's Heisman Trophy contenders: Miami has a nice two-week run where its opponents and the stage will allow for quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney to receive a big-time spotlight in the national conversation. This week's game against North Carolina, on Halloween night in Chapel Hill, will draw plenty of attention and could allow the Hurricanes (who are 14-point favorites) to continue building the resumes of both Mensah and Toney. Mensah is putting together one of the best starts to a season we have seen from a quarterback this century, currently leading the nation in completion percentage (81.4%) while also rolling up 22 passing touchdowns (2nd in FBS) and 307.3 passing yards per game (fourth in FBS). Malachi Toney, meanwhile, leads the FBS in receptions (66) and has become the first wide receiver with at least 900 receiving yards and 10 receiving touchdowns on a 7-0 team since eventual Heisman winner DeVonta Smith in 2020. Miami is elite in the middle (of games): It's easy to look at the collection of talent Mario Cristobal has assembled as an explanation for the team's dominance, but that talent has to perform to deliver the kind of results the Hurricanes have been getting over the last two seasons. Part of winning big has been winning small, and for Miami that's included dominating the middle portions of games. The Hurricanes have the No. 1 point differential in the second quarter in all of FBS (+95) and No. 3 point differential in the third quarter (+57). Miami is also No. 3 nationally this season in "middle 8" scoring (the last four minutes of the second quarter and the first four minutes of the third quarter), with a +7.6-point average on the season. Where to watch Miami vs. North Carolina live Date : Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Kenan Stadium -- Chapel Hill, N.C. TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. North Carolina prediction, picks Miami's first season of ACC play featured a trip to Chapel Hill on Halloween night to take on a North Carolina team that was 3-4 overall, with four 20-plus-point losses to ranked teams. The Hurricanes, ranked No. 4 at the time, were 6-0 and looking to establish themselves as the class of the ACC, having joined the conference just a few years removed from a national championship. A lot has been made about Miami's struggles in the last five meetings, but the Hurricanes' issues with the Heels date back to the very beginning of their time in the league, and Connor Barth's game-winning kick to seal the spooky upset. Bill Belichick and North Carolina's defense can get enough stops to keep this close, and with Notre Dame on deck, the Hurricanes might not be in the mindset to push this game deep into the evening. We're projecting North Carolina to flirt with the cover, but ultimately for the total to come in under the oddsmaker's number. away.headline: Miami gets concerning Malachi Toney injury update ahead of Notre Dame clash
away.blurb: Miami will undoubtedly want Toney available for this crucial matchup, but playing through an ankle injury could bring risks for one of the Hurricanes’ most valuable offensive weapons. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. Miami enters the matchup ranked No. 1 in both the AP Top 25 poll and the initial CFP rankings. Much of that has been thanks to the on-field brilliance of quarterback Darian Mensah and star wide receiver Malachi Toney. However, a concerning injury update regarding Toney surfaced on Wednesday, potentially putting his availability for the Notre Dame matchup in jeopardy. According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , sources told him and Max Olson that the Hurricanes’ Toney is dealing with an ankle injury, leaving his status for Saturday’s matchup “uncertain.” “Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game,” Thamel also said in his X report. More news: CFP Committee Chair Under Fire for Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Toney ranks second in NCAA football with 73 receptions, third with 1,027 receiving yards, and third with 13 touchdowns. The 5-foot-11 sophomore has delivered several impressive performances this past season, including 154 yards and two touchdowns in Miami’s double-overtime win over Florida State. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. However, several games remain on their schedules before the playoff field is finalized. A loss could seriously damage Notre Dame’s chances of getting into the College Football Playoff. Meanwhile, Miami is undefeated, and a loss could hurt its standing in the CFP rankings. Keeping that perfect record could strengthen Miami’s chances of a first-round bye in the CFP. The Miami Hurricanes take on the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. away.headline: The latest injury news on a key Hurricanes player who’s been out nearly all season
away.blurb: Over the last three games in particular — wins over Florida State, Pittsburgh and North Carolina — Miami’s pass defense given up an average of 326.7 passing yards per game. Overall, Miami ranks 112th out of 138 Football Bowl Subdivision teams in passing yards allowed per game (251.9). The Hurricanes have also given up 13 passing touchdowns while hauling in only four interceptions. Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal, speaking Monday ahead of Miami’s marquee game against the No. 4 Notre Dame Fighting Irish, said it will “still be a while” before Frederique returns to game action after getting hurt on the opening drive of Miami’s season opener against Stanford on Sept. 4. “Still looking at the latter portion of the season and maybe beyond if we’re fortunate enough to extend our season,” Cristobal said. Frederique started alongside Xavier Lucas at outside cornerback against Stanford but left after just two plays with an apparent shoulder injury after making an open-field tackle on the Cardinal’s Benji Blackburn on the opening drive of the eventual 45-6 Miami win . The St. Thomas Aquinas alumnus was one of the Hurricanes’ most dependable defenders during his first two seasons. He had 50 tackles and 14 pass breakups and an interception across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, although he did miss five games last year. UM’s secondary has dealt with injuries and poor performance throughout the season. Lucas missed three games after also getting hurt against Stanford, and a key reserve in sophomore Ja’Boree Antoine hasn’t played at all following an injury sustained during fall camp. away.blurb: REPORTS: Miami Hurricanes star WR Malachi Toney injured in practice; will have surgery | State of The U Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Miami Hurricanes Community State of The U November 5, 2026 State of The U Notifications Notifications The Feed FanDuel College Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Miami Hurricanes 2014 Recruiting Class Miami Hurricanes 2013 Recruiting Class Sections Expand Recruiting News Library Expand Miami Hurricanes 2014 Recruiting Class Notifications Miami Hurricanes Football A major developing story has emerged for the Hurricanes Per Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports, Malachi Toney is expected to undergo surgery for the ankle injury sustained today in practice. The injury is not thought to be season-ending, per the report. Ross Dellenger from Yahoo! Sports further reports that Toney is expected to miss 4-6 weeks recovering from this surgery. Additional reports from The Athletic, On3, and other outlets followed. The University of Miami has not released any statement regarding this injury at this time. It’s been a while since I wrote a report update kind of piece, but this one is necessary, unfortunately. There were multiple reports on Wednesday morning that Miami Hurricanes WR Malachi Toney sustained an ankle/lower leg injury during today’s practice. Initial reports indicated the injury was minor and Toney’s recovery would be minimal and his availability for this week’s game at Notre Dame was certain. However, further reports after Toney was further evaluated by medical professionals had a less positive outlook. The extent of Toney’s injury is not known. Since this week’s game is a non-conference game, there is no availability report that would give further insight. And, with Miami and Notre Dame both being private schools, they do not have to disclose such information publicly, should they choose not to. A leading Heisman Trophy candidate and the explosive element of Miami’s offense, Toney is among the best players not only at his position, but in the country. He’s already broken multiple records in his career at Miami, and very well may leave as the most productive player in program history. So, missing someone of that caliber would be a big loss for the Canes for any game, but especially one against a team of Notre Dame’s quality. This is a developing situation, and further updates will come when more is known. For now, the pretty well worked consensus is that Toney was injured today in practice and it was to his ankle/lower leg. Beyond that, we’ll have to wait and see. picks.blurb: Ohio State On SI Week 9 Picks: Can Buckeyes Overcome Spooky Road Test vs. USC? Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB Happy Halloween, Ohio State fans . The Buckeyes (6-1, 4-0 Big Ten) will try to maintain their No. 2 ranking Saturday night and attempt to knock off a desperate USC Trojans (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten) team still fighting for their CFP lives. With kickoff drawing closer, how does a Buckeyes team no longer led by quarterback Julian Sayin fare on the road? Scroll to find this week’s staff predictions, as I am all alone in first place at 7-0 so far this season. Ohio State @ USC Week 9 Game Details Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Parris Campbell (21) runs the ball as USC Trojans cornerback Isaiah Langley (24) tackles during the third quarter of the Goodyear Cotton Bowl Classic between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the USC Trojans on Friday, December 29, 2017 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. [Joshua A. Bickel/Dispatch] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT TV Channel: NBC (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds : Ohio State -6.5 ; over/under is 51.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum – Los Angeles, Calif. Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 88-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. USC: 2017 Cotton Bowl: Ohio State won 24-7, when the Trojans were still members of the Pac-12. USC leads the all-time series 13-10-1 since 1937. Ohio State so far this season: 6-1 (4-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando : 7-0 Dylan Buganski : 6-1 Rafael Zamorano : 4-1 (no pick in Week 6 or Week 7) Chip Minnich : 5-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 21, USC 17 After a week off, Ohio State continues its quest for a Big Ten and national title. It’ll just be without Julian Sayin as its starting quarterback. Since Sayin went down, Ohio State on SI (and I included) have done our best to bring Buckeye Nation as many perspectives as possible as the season resumes Saturday night in Los Angeles against the USC Trojans. Given the parity in this year's wacky college football season, the Buckeyes have yet to have a true reality-check moment. This week isn’t it either. The Badgers, who play the Iowa Hawkeyes earlier in the day’s action, suffocated the Trojans in all areas last week in Madison in one of the sport’s most shocking upsets. Although Halloween night could call for a spooky outcome (pun purposely intended), it’s hard to pick against Ohio State in Big Ten play, regardless of who the quarterback ends up being, until it loses in league play. So far, I’m the lone undefeated picker this season, so riding the hot hand with coach Ryan Day’s team against a depleted Trojans bunch seems like a smart pick (although all-time series history says otherwise). Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 24, USC 14 Ohio State has reached the crux of its season, not necessarily because of where they stand in Big Ten competition at this point in its schedule, but because we don’t know for sure what the Buckeyes will look like without star quarterback Julian Sayin for the foreseeable future. Not to take anything away from the 6-2 Trojans, but what was originally supposed to be a road game against a solid-but-not-elite conference opponent has now shifted its focus entirely on how the Buckeyes will look with a freshman starting at quarterback, be it true freshman Luke Fahey or redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair. Having said that, Ohio State still wields a deeper and more talented roster overall, headlined by the best player in the game, wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. The Buckeyes’ staff has more than enough resources to work with to keep whichever quarterback ends up starting well protected scheme-wise. Look for a lot of quick passes and screens on offense, while the defense figures out a way to pressure Jayden Maiava into committing mistakes, just like Wisconsin did last week. With the Buckeyes being favored by a touchdown on the spread (-7), I’m picking them to cover thanks to another solid performance on defense. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 24, USC 21 The Wisconsin Badgers’ 24-7 win over USC last Saturday has Ohio State fans understandably wondering whether the Buckeyes will follow a comparable game plan. I am guessing that Luke Fahey will be the starting quarterback, and that the coaching staff has emphasized to Fahey to play efficiently in a style reminiscent of when Julian Sayin made his first start at home vs. Texas in 2025. The USC defensive line has the pass rushing ability to get after an opposing quarterback, and I believe Fahey will use his legs to get out of the pocket and make positive yards to keep drives alive. Ohio State's defense is going to be tested all game against a formidable USC offense, despite the issues that the Trojans had last week in Madison. Maybe it's wishful thinking on my part, but this game has some serious Tresselball vibes for me going into Saturday night against an USC team that has its back to the wall. Yards and points may be difficult for the Buckeyes to earn, but I believe the Buckeyes will exhale when Connor Hawkins makes a late field goal in the final minutes of the contest. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, USC 14 For the first time during Ryan Day’s tenure as Ohio State head coach, a backup quarterback will start for the Buckeyes in a Big Ten matchup. It is still unknown if that starter will be true freshman Luke Fahey, or former 5-star sophomore Tavien St. Clair. Although, what is known coming into this matchup is that the USC defense has been one of the worst defenses against the pass in the Big Ten this season. Learning curves should be there for whatever quarterback is penciled to start in Los Angeles against the Trojans, but Heisman favorite Jeremiah Smith and the other pass-catchers in this room should still perform well and keep the Buckeye offense afloat. The run game will also be watched closely, as more will be expected from this group and it'll get a good test against a strong USC front. USC quarterback Jayden Maiava should make some plays to keep this game competitive, but expect the Ohio State front to stifle an inconsistent rushing attack from the Trojans and force some turnovers to swing the momentum in the Buckeyes’ favor, giving them their 6th straight win and first at USC since 1946. TOP PICK Who will win Ohio State vs USC: Ohio State -6.5 Although Ryan Day hasn't made it official, it appears that true freshman Luke Fahey will be making his first start for Ohio State against USC. Even with the precarious QB situation, I would take the Buckeyes to cover up to -8.5 on the road against the Trojans. USC might be at an all-time low in the Lincoln Riley era after scoring just seven points and totaling 239 yards in a 17-point loss to Wisconsin last week, a game the Trojans were favored in. If USC's offense can't compete against top defenses, and Ohio State's is arguably the best (ranked No. 1 by SP+ ), Riley's team doesn't stand a chance. USC's defense has been atrocious under Gary Patterson, ranking 96th in success rate (46%) . Fahey and Jeremiah Smith , the Heisman Trophy odds- favorite , should make enough plays to win a low-scoring game by nine or more points. Ohio State vs USC Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 USC's whole deal under Riley has been about having a strong enough offense to make up for poor defensive play. That hasn't been the case against quality programs, and this is USC's first taste of playing the Buckeyes since Riley took over. With Ohio State allowing just 13.4 points per game and holding six of seven opponents to fewer than 20 points, I like the Under at 49.5 or better . The Buckeyes' defense ranks fifth nationally in success rate (36.4%) , and USC is coming off an ugly outing against a Wisconsin defense that's a tier below the Buckeyes. But this is among the highest-ranked games in my Top 25 predictions this week because of Ohio State's QB situation. The Trojans have no run game and are asking too much of freshmen to carry the passing attack. Even if this game is tight heading into the fourth quarter, the Buckeyes will pull away. Memorial Coliseum on Saturday evening. Despite losing star quarterback Julian Sayin for the remainder of the season due to injury, Ohio State remains a 6.5-point road favorite to reign supreme over Lincoln Riley's Trojans. Below, I will break down this Week 9 matchup and provide the betting angles for a same-game parlay that you can take when wagering on Saturday's action! So, here are my USC vs. Ohio State picks and college football parlay for college football Week 9 on Saturday, October 31. Ohio State ML (-245) Jeremiah Smith 90+ Receiving Yards (-185) Parlay Odds: +126 ( DraftKings ) Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . USC vs Ohio State Odds For the first leg of our SGP for Saturday night's conference clash, I feel confident backing Ryan Day's Buckeyes on the moneyline in what could be a closely contested game down the stretch. While the Trojans stock took a major hit this past weekend when Lincoln Riley's bunch got embarrassed by Wisconsin by 17 points in Madison, USC still boasts an elite offense led by quarterback Jayden Maiava — one of the best players in all of college football. Though most were extremely high on Julian Sayin prior to his season-ending injury , I was always under the impression that he was a tad overrated, with a great deal of his success resulting from an elite offensive line and freakish playmaker in wide receiver Jeremiah Smith . While a decision has yet to be made on who will be starting for the Buckeyes under center on Saturday night, we do know that Day will be choosing between Luke Fahey and Tavien St Clair. Both QBs were extremely highly touted coming out of high school, and while it may take some time to adjust to the college game, this is still an Ohio State team that's far superior to USC on both sides of the football. Sure, the Trojans boast an elite offensive unit and now hold a definitive edge at the QB position, but this is a USC program that has dropped the ball in huge games time and again. Despite the uncertainty under center, Ohio State is the far more reliable team of the two, and I would be surprised if it didn't leave the Coliseum with an outright victory on Saturday night. Given Sayin's season-ending injury, we're provided with a rare opportunity to back Ohio State's generational receiver in Jeremiah Smith at a discount — and that's exactly what I'll be buying into. For a program consistently churning out elite receivers, including the likes of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Chris Olave, Smith still may be the most talented offensive player to ever suit up in Columbus. The junior wideout has already racked up 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns thus far, and I don't expect his elite production to take as big a hit as betting markets appear to suggest. Smith is still the best player in all of college football, and I feel great backing the Buckeyes' phenom to record at least 90 receiving yards on Saturday night at -185. picks.blurb: Final Pick and Prediction for Ohio State and USC's Primetime Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Final Pick and Prediction for Ohio State and USC's Primetime Matchup Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's been a long two weeks in between Ohio State's last two games, and the wait is finally over as tonight the Buckeyes finally get to take on the USC Trojans inside the Los Angeles Coliseum. The storylines are vast on both sides, with the main one being injuries on both sides. The Buckeyes are obviously down Julian Sayin on their offense, while the Trojans have a couple of injuries, but none to key contributors on their team. The good news for Ohio State is that while Sayin is out, he doesn't play defense, and Jeremiah Smith is 100 percent ready to go. As long as those two things stay true, the Buckeyes could roll me out at quarterback and have a really good chance to win the football game, especially this one. As it stands right now, the Buckeyes are a one-touchdown favorite against the Trojans by 6.5 points. Nearly the entire public is on the Buckeyes, and for good reason. The performance that USC rolled out last week was a regrettable one for sure. They went all the way across the country to Madison, Wisconsin, to take on the Badgers, and they got an old-school beatdown as a result. From start to finish, the Badgers controlled the physicality of the football game and never allowed the Trojans to get off the mat at all. They forced turnovers, stopped the run, and made USC get into chase mode. They did all of that while registering just 54 passing yards on the game. Ohio State Bye Week: How Are the Buckeyes Going to Approach Life After Julian SayinWe are back on the Buckeye Breakdown Podcast on Ohio State's bye week. No action for the Buckeyes on Saturday, but it was the biggest week of their season as... That could not have happened at a better time for the Buckeyes because it is the exact blueprint that they are going to want to create in this game. The Buckeyes' defense is proving that it is one of the best in the country by far and away. After they figured out some of the negatives in their group against the Illinois Fighting Illini, they have looked totally different. They turned the water off against Iowa, Maryland, and Indiana. They have reverted to their old form, and it is happening at the right time. On offense, they will have their five best offensive lineman up and ready to go today. That group has been a revolving door all year long, but they are the ones that benefited the most from the bye week. They are back to full strength, and the Ohio State rushing attack is going to benefit from that. Finally, No. 4 still plays for the Buckeyes last time that I checked. Anytime you have Jeremiah Smith on your side, you have more than a chance. This is going to be a fast game, one that the Buckeyes choke the clock out, control time of possession, protect their young quarterback, and just try to escape with a win, and I think that they will, easily. The final prediction in this one is Ohio State 24, USC 10. Buckeyes come back home as the No. 2 team in the country with Oregon next up.

One of the more intriguing matchups on the Week 9 college football calendar finds the Buckeyes going on the road against the Trojans without Julian Sayin under center. How does that affect what happens in this battle of college football blue bloods? How Ohio State can win Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates a touchdown with with wide receiver Devin McCuin (3) during the NCAA football game against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. on Oct. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Regardless of concerns at quarterback, Ohio State has the more complete statistical profile, particularly on defense. The Buckeyes are allowing just 13.4 points and 264.3 total yards per game, ranking fourth and sixth nationally, respectively. Their run defense has been especially effective, giving up only 92.9 rushing yards per game. It should have a decisive edge against a USC ground game that is 105th in FBS and totaling just 131 yards on average. Offensively, Jeremiah Smith has been spectacular yet again. The undefendable wide receiver and Heisman favorite has 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns on 52 catches. Even without Sayin, Ohio State can lean on its defense, establish Bo Jackson in the trenches, slow the game down, get the football into Smith's hands, and let him create after the catch. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Maybe relying on USC's defense to win a game hasn't always been a great idea. But they're in a very good position to exploit the Buckeyes' uncertainty at quarterback. Applying enough pressure on the edges to rattle Sayin's replacement could give this talented offense enough breathing room to make this interesting. The Trojans are averaging 303.6 passing yards per game, ranking 10th nationally, with quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing for 2,303 yards and 19 touchdowns. USC also converts 50.5 percent of its third downs, the 14th-best rate in the country. That ability to sustain drives could be important against an Ohio State defense that has allowed opponents to convert just 38 percent of third downs. The Trojans need Maiava to protect the football and attack downfield over top OSU's front line defenders. Defensively, USC must pressure the inexperienced Buckeyes quarterback and prevent him from developing any early rhythm. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 9's biggest games Who wins, and why? Make no mistake: the absence of Julian Sayin distributing to the Buckeyes' talented wideouts is a real problem. USC, whatever its defensive lapses in the Riley era, has a legitimate opportunity to make this uncomfortable. Still, Ohio State has a significant defensive advantage overall, allowing just 13 points per game and has an important edge countering the Trojans' ground game that can reduce that offense to one dimension. USC will have opportunities, but Ohio State's defensive consistency ultimately proves to be the edge in the second half. The Big Lead prediction: Ohio State 30, USC 23

picks.blurb: Drake London drops USC prediction for big Ohio State clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Drake London drops USC prediction for big Ohio State clash Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Sat, October 31, 2026 at 10:32 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The USC Trojans face a make or break game Saturday night when they host the second-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes. The Trojans are coming off a disappointing 24-7 home loss to Wisconsin, and Lincoln Reilly's team is going to have to come up with a much better effort against one of the nation's powerhouse teams. Ohio State is playing its first game without starting quarterback Julian Sayin. He suffered an arm injury in Ohio State's 19-15 victory at Indiana earlier in October. Head coach Ryan Day did not name a starter until late Friday when it was revealed that Luke Fahey would be under center instead of Tavien St. Clair. While the Buckeyes have Heisman Trophy favorite Jeremiah Smith at wide receiver and a slew of talented pass catchers, it doesn't seem likely that they will ask Fahey to win the game for them. However, it is clear that the 6.5-point road favorites are asking him not to lose the game. Former USC star Drake London , currently the Atlanta Falcons' top receiver, believes the Trojans have a great chance to come up with the upset. picks.headline: ESPN’s computer model reveals bold prediction for Ohio State-USC game
picks.blurb: ESPN’s computer model reveals bold prediction for Ohio State-USC game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings ESPN’s computer model reveals bold prediction for Ohio State-USC game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Ohio State had a full week to come up with a plan to replace its starting quarterback. Whatever it does should be more than enough to handle a road test at USC on Saturday. That's the opinion of the College Football Power Index. ESPN's algorithmic prediction model sounds very confident in what the Buckeyes can accomplish against the Trojans, even with a new face at the quarterback position. FPI projects Buckeyes will dominate Trojans Oct 17, 2026; Bloomington, Indiana, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) walks off the field with his arm in a sling after the game against the Indiana Hoosiers Merchants Bank Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The computer model, which simulates games 20,000 times, projects Ohio State to be 13.4 points better than USC . That's a surprisingly sizable margin for a team heading into a road game without star Julian Sayin. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 9 The Buckeyes remain one of college football 's strongest teams, but their quarterback uncertainty makes that projection particularly bold ahead of Saturday's matchup at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Sayin's absence remains the biggest concern after the quarterback suffered a throwing-arm injury during Ohio State's 19-15 victory over Indiana on Oct. 17. Sayin, who threw for 2,007 yards and 19 touchdowns this season, is expected to be out indefinitely. Who's on deck for the Buckeyes? The uncertainty is compounded by the fact that head coach Ryan Day has not officially named a starter. As of Thursday, both freshman Luke Fahey and redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair were preparing to play against USC. Fahey has completed nine of 13 passes for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions; St. Clair has attempted only seven passes. Neither has demonstrated that he can sustain an offense over a full game against a quality opponent. Trojans can test Ohio State's defense Southern California Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) throws against the Northwestern Wildcats during the second half at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images USC also has a capable offense of its own. Quarterback Jayden Maiava has thrown for 2,303 yards and 19 touchdowns, while the Trojans average 32.8 points per game. Although USC is coming off a 24–7 loss to Wisconsin, its passing game could test Ohio State's defense if the Buckeyes struggle to maintain possession on the other side. The counterargument is Ohio State's defense, which allows just 13.4 points per game, and the presence of star receiver Jeremiah Smith. The Heisman favorite has 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns. Those strengths help explain why the Buckeyes remain heavily favored by predictive models. Still, a 13-point projection assumes Ohio State can maintain much of its usual efficiency despite a major change at the sport's most important position. Until Fahey or St. Clair proves capable of directing the offense for four quarters, that margin looks ambitious. Ohio State is still the better team, but expecting the Buckeyes to win comfortably in their first game without Sayin is a bold call.

away.headline: Ohio State football's Jay Timmons trending toward return against Oregon
away.blurb: Ohio State starting nickel back Jay Timmons is trending toward a return against Oregon on Nov. 7. Timmons, who was held out of last week’s loss at USC with an unspecified injury, was not included on the Buckeyes’ initial availability report released for their upcoming game against the Ducks. Timmons missed games against Iowa and Maryland earlier in October before returning at Indiana when he reaggravated his injury. He traveled with the Buckeyes to Los Angeles last week as he attempted to return but was ruled out near kickoff. Wide receivers Brock Boyd and Brandon Inniss were listed as questionable for Oregon after they were held out at USC. It was the second straight game Boyd was sidelined with an unspecified injury. Left tackle Ian Moore was also listed as questionable. Moore made a late exit against the Trojans as Austin Siereveld moved over from right tackle to replace him in the fourth quarter. Defensive tackle Eddrick Houston was not listed after he went down late last week and later limped off the field at the Coliseum, indicating he could be available against Oregon. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State football's Jay Timmons trending toward return against Oregon He has also practiced in recent days, prompting coach Ryan Day to express optimism about his status on Nov. 4. “We’ll have to see how the next 48 hours go,” Day said, “but he’s had two good days of practice. That would really inject a lot for us in the back end.” The Buckeyes’ secondary felt the absence of Timmons against the Trojans as they surrendered their longest passes this season between a 69-yard touchdown on the second play from scrimmage and another 70-yard reception in the third quarter. home.headline: USC Trojans star JuJu Watkins gets emotional after first game back from injury
home.blurb: JuJu Watkins didn’t hold back her emotions after ending a 588-day absence by making her return from injury in the No. 3 USC Trojans’ 100-68 blowout win over the UNLV Rebels on Monday night. Watkins prepared herself to return in full force, which she successfully pulled off. In 25 minutes of action, she finished with a stat line of 21 points, five rebounds, two assists, and two steals. She shot 9-of-22 from the field and 3-of-4 from the free-throw line. She reflected on her return from injury after the game, expressing immense gratitude that she got to come back to the court with her teammates. “It was great to just be out there with my team again, and to see the first one fall through. It really helped. So yeah, just grateful to be out here today,” Watkins said on the CBS broadcast. “I’m most proud of just my consistency. Like there were days where I could have given up, and so I kept pushing through. And I’m just grateful that I’m here.” JuJu Watkins is on a mission to return to form as one of the best players in the country. She has a promising future ahead of her in the pros, needing to deliver great performances to show she has successfully come back from the severe injury. Related: USC women’s basketball news: Trojans pull off extremely rare feat in JuJu Watkins’ return Watkins started the fourth season of her collegiate career with the Trojans, the third that sees her on the court. She suffered a torn ACL during the second round of the 2025 NCAA Tournament, an injury that sidelined her for the entire 2025-26 campaign. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) How JuJu Watkins, USC played against UNLV Five players scored in double-digits for USC in the win, including Watkins. Jazz Davidson led the team with 23 points, five rebounds, four assists, and two steals. She shot 10-of-11 overall, including 1-of-2 from downtown. Saniyah Hall came next with 22 points and seven rebounds, Kennedy Smith had 12 points and four steals, while Sitaya Fagan provided 11 points and three assists. The Lady Trojans will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Utah State Aggies as tip-off commences on Nov. 8 at 8 p.m. ET. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Helwick · SB Nation Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:12 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, October 30 at 7:30 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: Baylor (-1.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Baylor leads, 2-1 Last meeting: Baylor 30, UCF 3 — November 1, 2025 Current streak: Baylor, 2 (2023-25) Setting the scene Baylor and UCF have only met three times, but there is no shortage of iconic moments between these programs. UCF entered the 2013 Fiesta Bowl as a 13.5-point underdog to Big 12 champion Baylor. However, Blake Bortles led the Knights to an electrifying 52-42 victory on New Year's Day, sealing the program's first-ever AP Top 10 finish. Ten years later, UCF held a 35-7 lead in the late third quarter over Baylor, but the Bears rallied with 29 unanswered, surviving a wild fourth down conversion and a 59-yard field goal attempt to hold onto a 36-35 win. Perhaps another memorable finish awaits as the programs meet in Orlando for the 10th annual Space Game. UCF continues one of college football's most recognizable modern traditions, rebranding to the "Citronauts" for a night and donning space-themed alternate uniforms as a nod to the university's aeronautical roots. The Citronauts are one of the better teams in college football history, owning an 8-1 record in Space Games and outscoring opponents by an aggregate result of 432-189: 2017 – UCF 63, East Carolina 21 2018 – UCF 52, Temple 40 2019 – UCF 44, Houston 29 2020 – UCF 51, Tulane 34 2021 – UCF 24, Memphis 7 2022 – UCF 70, Temple 13 2023 – UCF 45, Oklahoma State 3 2024 – UCF 56, Arizona 12 2025 – Houston 30, UCF 27 However, Houston defeated UCF in last year's Space Game, spoiling the Citronauts' perfect record. UCF, coming off its first top-5 victory in program history, aims to recapture its galactic momentum as Baylor strolls into the Bounce House. Baylor Bears outlook WACO, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19: Defensive Coordinator Joe Klanderman of the Baylor Bears yells from the sideline during the second quarter during the game against the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs on September 19, 2026 at the McLane Stadium in Waco, Texas. (Photo by Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) fired head coach Dave Aranda in the middle of his seventh season in Waco. Aranda's tenure was quite volatile, featuring highs of a 12-2 finish and Big 12 championship in 2021, but lows including a 3-9 record in 2023. The Bears lacked consistency under Aranda, improving or declining by at least three wins in every year from 2019 through 2025. Baylor moves forward with interim Joe Klanderman, who also retains his defensive coordinator duties. In year one on campus, Klanderman has done a stellar job reforming Baylor's defense. He implemented a 3-3-5 base scheme and vastly improved the unit, allowing them to skyrocket from 122nd to 19th in scoring defense and 122nd to 22nd in run defense. The Bears let up just 16.1 points per game, and last Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas was the first time they surrendered more than 17 points all season. The defense showed promise even in losing efforts, falling 17-16 to Auburn and 17-6 to TCU. Baylor is the best in the Big 12 at getting to the quarterback and its 3.9 sacks per game rank third nationally. There isn't one dominant pass rusher, rather, it's a concerted effort. Edge rusher Garrick Ponder leads the charge with 4.0 sacks while safeties Daniel Cobbs and Bo Onu are tied for second with 3.0 apiece. With great pressure comes great chaos, and Baylor is producing takeaways at a high rate. The team ranks 15th nationally with 13 takeaways, and strong safety Micah Gifford has been omnipresent with three interceptions and two fumble recoveries. While the passing defense has more interceptions than touchdowns allowed, and forces opponents to a 59.8 completion rate, Baylor still allows 236 passing yards per game, which ranks 103rd nationally. Teams regularly hit explosives on the Bears, which have given up 13 passes of 30 yards or greater through seven games. Last season, Baylor excelled offensively and struggled on defense. This year, the opposite is true. Outside of the 55-19 rout at Arizona State, the Bears have not been able to consistently generate points. They scored 24 or fewer points in four of seven games, and all three losses were attribute to a lack of scoring. Still, quarterback DJ Lagway has moved the ball well for the nation's 24th-ranked passing offense. The veteran starter averages 270 passing yards per game, delivering nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Efficiency has been an issue through the air though, and Baylor checks in at 124th in the FBS with a 56.4 completion rate. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman operates as the main target. His 58 receptions are the second-most in the country and his 678 receiving yards rank second in the Big 12. Louis Brown and Jayden McGowan are among Lagway's other frequented options. Baylor hasn't been as lethal on the ground, still awaiting its first 90-yard rusher of the season. The Bears were held to 54 rushing yards against TCU and 122 against Kansas — a significant reason Baylor enters Orlando on a two-game losing streak. UCF Knights outlook ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights celebrates a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) is coming off a win for the ages. Although the Knights won multiple New Year's Six bowls and secured an NCAA-recognized national championship in 2017, last Saturday's double overtime triumph over No. 2 BYU was the program's first-ever top-5 victory in history. It was the long-awaited signature win of Scott Frost's second tenure in Orlando and restored energy into a fanbase, which will certainly show up in droves for the annual Space Game. There were moments throughout the BYU game where it appeared UCF missed a golden opportunity for an upset. However, the Knights stayed the course and won just their second October game in their last 13 tries. One of the heroes last week was quarterback Keyone Jenkins, who threw for 293 yards and three touchdowns, while rushing for an additional score in the 39-31 win. After witnessing several strong performances by the FIU transfer, Frost named Jenkins the starting quarterback moving forward, even though original starter Alonza Barnett III has recovered from a Week 2 hamstring injury. UCF has received stronger support from the passing attack in recent weeks, which has been efficient. The Knights have thrown 13 touchdowns against four interceptions, while completing 66.5 percent of attempts this year. It hasn't been the most explosive unit, completing just seven passes spanning 30 yards and two spanning 40, but Jenkins has allowed the Knights to piece together methodical possessions. The run game has been the hallmark of UCF's offense all season. Running back Duke Watson is eighth in the Big 12 in rushing and averages 6.8 yards per carry. Landen Chambers has also stepped up from the backfield lately, scoring two touchdowns in last week's win over BYU. But the true emerging star in UCF's offense is true freshman wide receiver Tyren Hornes. After being underutilized in September, Hornes has become one of the top options for the Knights, producing 137 yards on six receptions last Saturday. He now ranks second on the team in receiving yards behind Josh Derry, who leads all Knight receivers in catches (34), yards (358), and touchdowns (3). Although the last two weeks were more offensive oriented games, UCF has been best on the defensive side this year. The Knights allow 23.0 points per game, allow just 3.2 yards per rushing attempt, and hold opponents to a completion rate of 58.9 percent. However, UCF must play the Space Game without arguably its best defensive player. Strong safety Demari Henderson suffered an injury in overtime against BYU, and the team will miss his production, which includes 35 tackles, two interceptions, and five pass breakups. The Knights still have several veteran faces in the secondary including cornerbacks Antione Jackson and Jayden Bellamy, who both have one interception and one forced fumble on the season. Thanks to these defensive backs, UCF is a plus-5 in the turnover battle this season. Can UCF avoid a letdown after an emotional win? Signature wins haven't been easy to follow up in college football this season. Auburn beat Georgia and then lost by 21 to LSU at home. BYU took down Notre Dame and then dropped an overtime thriller to UCF a week later. Ole Miss' triumph over LSU was followed by a thrashing at the hands of Florida. And so on. Baylor also had an eventful week, as the Bears move on from head coach Dave Aranda and now must respond with an interim head coach in a hostile Orlando environment. The Bears' defense has been consistently sound this year, and UCF may struggle to come close to its Space Game average of 48 points per game. The defenses control this matchup, and the Bears prevent a successful launch with a game-winning field goal in the final minute. Prediction: Baylor 24, UCF 21

picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals UCF Can UCF recapture Space Game magic vs. Baylor? Picks, scouting report Chris Boyle Daytona Beach News-Journal Updated Oct. 30, 2026, 10:48 a.m. ET UCF is set to host Baylor for its 10th annual Space Game after a stunning upset victory over BYU. Baylor recently parted ways with head coach Dave Aranda, with defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman taking over as interim. The Knights will wear special all-white uniforms as a tribute to 1960s astronauts for the game. ORLANDO — UCF stole the national spotlight last weekend with its stunning upset of then-No. 2 BYU . More than 4.7 million viewers tuned in as the Knights prevailed 39-31 in double overtime, FOX's most-watched afternoon college football game in two years. The Knights get another prime-time opportunity in the Acrisure Bounce House on Oct. 30, albeit against a reeling Big 12 rival suddenly without its head coach. UCF (4-3, 2-2) hosts Baylor (4-3, 2-2) for its 10th annual Space Game at 7:30 p.m. on ESPN. The visiting Bears parted ways with Dave Aranda in the middle of his seventh season in charge following their 25-24 loss at Kansas, their second successive defeat. The Knights will ditch their traditional black and gold uniforms for an all-white homage to 1960s astronauts . UCF is 8-1 all-time in Space Games, though its first loss occurred last November — a 30-27 defeat to Houston that effectively ended its hopes at bowl eligibility. "There are so many neat aspects to UCF, where we came from and what we stand for and things that other schools don't have," Knights head coach Scott Frost said. "I like how we're pouring into that and doubling down on that. Coming off the win that we had, and the fact that it's the Space Game, I hope there's a ton of fans. They were awesome after the (BYU) game. Hopefully, this gets a packed Bounce House for Friday night. We need to show up and play really hard." Can the Knights build upon the momentum, or will they crash back down to Earth? The News-Journal's trio of Chris Boyle, Chris Vinel and Ken Willis offer their analysis and score predictions. UCF vs. Baylor tale of the tape Keyone Jenkins earned Maxwell Award National Player of the Week and Davey O'Brien National Quarterback of the Week honors for his performance against BYU, throwing for 293 yards and accounting for four touchdowns. Frost named him the starter Oct. 26 with Alonza Barnett III still not 100% ready to play after suffering a hamstring injury six weeks ago. During the second overtime period, Jenkins was evaluated for a concussion and cleared, though he likely would not have been available if BYU tied the score. "He's the hot hand right now," Frost said. "I'm really pleased with Alonza's progress. I think he probably could play; I don't know if he's 100% yet. "I think the reps have really helped Keyone. He played a pretty special game Saturday and made plays when we needed to make them." Freshman wide receiver Tyren Hornes delivered a breakout performance with six catches for a game-high 137 yards, including a game-changing, 56-yard gain on a third-and-17 perimeter screen. Landen Chambers contributed a pair of touchdowns in regulation, and both Josh Derry and Grayson Brousseau caught one apiece during overtime. UCF is tied for 21st in the nation with a +5 turnover margin; linebacker Tackett Curtis generated the defense's 12th takeaway of the year with a first-half interception of Bear Bachmeier. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman assumes the head coaching duties for Baylor for the remainder of the season. He joined the program in January from Kansas State. Statistically, Baylor sits among the country's best defenses in a number of key metrics — tied for fifth in sacks (27), ninth in tackles for loss (59), tied for 15th in takeaways (13), 19th in scoring (16.1 ppg), 22nd against the run (104.1 ypg allowed) and 42nd in third-down conversion rate (34.8%). Florida transfer DJ Lagway is completing a career-low 52.1% of his passes, throwing for 1,352 yards with nine touchdowns and four interceptions. He thrived in a backup role against UCF in 2024, going 4-of-4 passing for 50 yards. Baylor's rushing offense is tied for 87th nationally with 146.1 yards per game — at 3.8 per carry. Gavin Freeman tops all Big 12 receivers with 58 catches, producing 678 yards with two touchdowns. Apopka native Travion Barnes paces the Bears with 51 tackles. Garrick Ponder is among the league's leaders in sacks (four) and TFLs (eight). UCF vs. Baylor scouting report: What we're watching Chris Boyle: Can the Knights force Lagway into errant throws and pick them off? Across two seasons in Gainesville, the former five-star recruit launched 23 interceptions — at a rate of roughly 4.3% of all attempts. He's thrown at least one pick in four of his five starts for Baylor, and the Bears are 2-3 in those contests. UCF's experienced defensive backs have not snagged a pick in more than a month. In fairness, they have gone up against three of the nation's premier signal-callers in Houston's Conner Weigman, Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Bachmeier. Lagway will likely give the Knights chances to make plays on the football, and they must take advantage. Chris Vinel: Will the Space Game have the same juice and appeal after the 2025 loss? UCF has never had to answer that question. Does the Knights' cosmic magic just go away? Or do they revert back to the juggernaut that was blowing out opponents by an average of 31 points through the first eight years of the tradition? One certainty: The 1960s-inspired alternate uniforms will look good. Ken Willis: Baylor administrators obviously had loftier plans for the Bears than the rest of us did. They fired a coach with a 4-3 record, which you'd expect in Tuscaloosa or Columbus, but certainly not Waco. Whatever, that's their business, but the fallout usually goes big, one way or the other. Do the Bears rally under an interim and try to prove a point of some sort? Or does the current two-game losing streak gain momentum? With today's itinerant rosters, there's probably not a lot of institutional pride in play with Baylor. Either way, UCF does have a say in all this, and instead of a letdown after beating BYU, I suspect a whiff of wind at the Knights' backs — until they go back on the road next week, of course. UCF vs. Baylor injury updates Barnett took pregame reps as the emergency backup last Saturday after being declared a game-time decision 90 minutes prior to kickoff. Jenkins' week-over-week improvements have allowed UCF's coaching staff to feel confident not needing to rush the James Madison transfer. Linebacker Lewis Carter, safety Demari Henderson and running back Taevion Swint were among five Knights ruled out on Tuesday's initial availability report. Swint will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury that occurred during practice last week. "Chick got hurt on a nothing play … It was rough to see," he added. "He was just slowing down, didn't turn his ankle or anything. Just started limping. I think we kind of figured out the injury was an old injury, so he'll be back quicker than we thought right after (it happened). I don't know yet about his status this week." As for Baylor, leading rusher Dawson Pendergrass and cornerback Devon Jordan are questionable for the game. Pendergrass, a senior, has 331 rushing yards and two touchdowns on the year. Jordan, a junior, has three interceptions, including a 42-yard pick-six in last week's loss at Kansas. Bears safety Jacob Redding required season-ending knee surgery prior to the team's neutral-site opener against Auburn in Atlanta. UCF vs. Baylor score predictions, picks Chris Boyle: UCF 23, Baylor 14 Chris Vinel: UCF 27, Baylor 20 Ken Willis: UCF 23, Baylor 20
