home.headline: UCF football has QB decision to make, if injuries don't make it first
home.blurb: The team built its offseason around the addition of Alonza Barnett III, a two-year starter at James Madison fresh off Sun Belt Conference Player of the Year honors and a trip to the College Football Playoff. Frost's staff protected its sizable financial investment in Barnett, holding him out of all 15 spring practice sessions as a precaution. Baylor's vaunted defensive front knocked Jenkins out in the third quarter of Friday's 41-9 defeat. Frost said the senior reaggravated an ankle problem, though the severity is unknown. Barnett returned from a five-game absence but could not provide the spark needed to ignite a comeback. UCF flip-flopped through four quarterbacks in 2025, Frost's return to Orlando after seven years - five as Nebraska's head coach. Plans changed two games into the campaign when Barnett sustained a "fairly significant" hamstring injury, sidelining him for more than a month. Keyone Jenkins, a 33-game starter at Florida International, stepped in and steadied the ship at the start of Big 12 play. He led the Knights to their highest-ranked win in program history Oct. 24, a 39-31 double-overtime classic against BYU, with 293 passing yards and four total touchdowns. However, seats could switch again for the stretch run after yet another injury. As November approaches, and with UCF needing another pair of wins to achieve bowl eligibility, uncertainty exists about the starting signal-caller going forward. "I've said a lot that I feel good about our quarterbacks, whoever's in there," Frost said. A familiar problem for UCF head coach Scott Frost Cam Fancher lasted less than a half before getting clobbered on a sack, injuring his back, and then sustained broken ribs at Cincinnati a month later. Tayven Jackson started 10 times, but battled several ailments, including a shoulder joint sprain at Kansas State. Jacurri Brown injured his shoulder in that same game and did not see the field the rest of the year. Fourth-stringer Davi Belfort, now a wide receiver at James Madison, made a few appearances, throwing a game-sealing interception in a loss to Houston. Thus, the root problem lies in the support system, as opposed to strictly a QB's individual performance or toughness. "Whoever was playing quarterback, it's going to be hard if we don't block better and create a running game," Frost said. "I mean, we couldn't get anything going in the first half. We couldn't get a run game going, and we didn't protect very well." He went 8-of-16 passing for 133 yards, finishing with five straight completions. home.headline: Kansas HC Lance Leipold Remains Noncommittal on Isaiah Marshall's Status vs. UCF
home.blurb: Many Kansas football fans are checked out with the state of the program after another grueling loss last week to TCU. However, the Jayhawks still have one-third of the campaign to go sitting at 3-5. In KU's most recent defeat, quarterback Isaiah Marshall was inactive for the first time this year due to a lower-leg injury. In his place, backup Cole Ballard returned to action after dealing with a shoulder ailment of his own. For the Jayhawks to realistically stay in the race for bowl eligibility this Saturday against UCF, they very much need Marshall to return under center. However, it remains far from a sure thing that the redshirt sophomore makes his way back to the field over the weekend. Head coach Lance Leipold remained noncommittal on his quarterback choice during his weekly press conference today. Marshall has been banged up since the start of the year, which isn't surprising given his lean frame and how involved he is in the rushing attack. Still, there was no indication that his status for the TCU contest was in jeopardy until he popped up on the injury report three days before kickoff. He was then downgraded to questionable and ultimately was held out for precautionary reasons as a game-time decision. home.headline: UCF Faced With Depleted Secondary For Kansas Road Trip: Injury Report Breakdown
home.blurb: This week, it's the defensive back room that has officially been hit with the injury bug, as a third player from it has been ruled out for the Knights' matchup against Kansas at 3:45 p.m. on Saturday. However, this week, UCF is not the only school in its matchup having a tough go against the injury bug, as the Jayhawks have a whopping nine players designated questionable and six ruled out . The Knights will be without multiple defensive backs for back-to-back weeks, with three being ruled out on Wednesday. Demari Henderson and DJ Bell are out again on Saturday, with Henderson missing his second game of the season and Bell his third. In Lawrence, Kahmel Johnson is also joining them on the sideline. Ty Bartrum , who was designated probable in Wednesday's report, was the main benficiary of Henderson being out for the Space Game, tallying nine tackles. Caleb Flagg also saw the field, making three tackles. With Bell once again out, Jayden Bellamy and Antione Jackson are once again faced with an increased snap share at cornerback. Though Jailen Duffi e and Rukeem Stroud are both there to back them up. While his name may not be on this week's player availability report, Frost said on Monday that Owen Spell , who started the season as UCF's starting right guard, is out for the regular season . Gibson has been ruled out , making the Kansas game the fourth consecutive missed game for the backup right tackle to Preston Cushman , leaving an opportunity for Laparka Langston , Justin Royes , Cooper Terpstra or Kasiyah Charlton to step into the role. However, Langston could already be spoken for on Saturday depending on the status of Maiava, who was ruled questionable on Wednesday. Frost said on Monday that while he did not know about his status for the Kansas game, he "avoided anything serious" with the injury he sustained during the Space Game. During the two games he was out for, Connor Meadows shifted to center while Langston started at right guard. Following Friday's Space Game, coach Scott Frost said Keyone Jenkins reaggravated an ankle injury he had been nursing for a few weeks, though he did not know how serious. He was designated questionable on Wednesday's report. Meanwhile, Alonza Barnett III , who stepped in for Jenkins on Friday and was declared healthy by Frost on Monday, has been ruled probable . One of those guys Frost is referring to is linebacker Jayden Jennings , who was designated as probable on Wednesday night.
